Several arrests have been made at an anti-immigration protest in Portsmouth on suspicion of criminal damage, obstructing a highway and wearing an item to conceal identity.

Hampshire Police said on Saturday that a 76-year-old man from Southampton was arrested on suspicion of wearing or using an item to conceal identity at a protest after the force announced it would use powers enabling it to arrest anybody wearing a face covering at the demonstration.

A person wearing what appeared to be black scarves tied across his face and head was pictured in handcuffs on Saturday afternoon.

A 33-year-old man from Portsmouth was also arrested on suspicion of obstructing a highway.

Earlier that day officers arrested a man on suspicion of criminal damage after a police van was targeted.

open image in gallery Demonstrators participate in an anti-migrant march in Portsmouth ( Getty )

An officer at the scene said the man was walking with a breakaway group after the majority of the protesters had dispersed.

Police also arrested a 16-year-old male from Portsmouth on suspicion of violent disorder, in relation to violent public disorder at Eastney Marina last Sunday, where crowds gathered after a dinghy’s arrival across the English Channel.

A line of police formed to keep anti-racism protesters from anti-immigration protesters who followed them as they were leaving the scene.

One man repeatedly yelling “scum”, while a woman in the anti-racism group replied “you’re threatening us”. Police warned earlier that they would not tolerate incitement of fear or violence as groups from South Coast Patriots and Stand up to Racism took to the streets to march.

Protesters were not wearing masks at either gathering after warnings from Hampshire and Isle of Wight Constabulary that anyone wearing face coverings could be arrested under powers in the Crime and Policing Act.

Police said the powers were aimed at preventing violence and disorder following protests in the city over the past week involving masked demonstrators.

One video posted to social media showed a man wearing a burqa, in an apparent attempt to flout the ban, being spoken to by police.

open image in gallery Masked demonstrators were seen at an anti-migrant protests in Portsmouth and Dover last weekend ( Getty )

Another man on a mobility scooter wearing a plastic face mask was stopped by police at the Guildhall Square in Portsmouth, where he was spoken to by officers. He then removed the mask and continued on his way.

A large police presence was seen in Portsmouth city centre where anti-migrant protesters were seen holding Union flags, while some wearing Portsmouth Patriot branded clothing were gathering outside All Saints Church on Commercial Road.

In the neighbouring car park, demonstrators holding Stand up to Racism and Refugees Welcome banners also gathered. Signs included “RNLI are heroes, no-one is illegal”, a reference to the abuse volunteers got when they helped escort migrants to safety last week.

A Section 60AA order will also be in place during the march, giving police officers the power to make protesters remove masks, face coverings, or any other items being used to conceal their identity.

Earlier, a member of the Facebook group The Patriots of Great Britain, urged anti-migrant protesters to wear “hats, shades and war paint” instead of face coverings in an apparent attempt to flout the ban.

“They can't ban those. It will show people not to be frightened of you, it will invoke British humour and pride, and it will give the right-wing media something to praise, and it will make the government look like mugs,” he added.

Another shared an AI-generated image of an army of men all wearing hats, sunglasses and beards, with the caption “where there’s a will, there’s a way”.

open image in gallery Protesters at Dover Priory train station after black-clad and masked anti-illegal migrant demonstrators blocked roads in Dover during a protest on 5 September ( PA )

The policing powers will be in force in Portsmouth from 9am on Saturday to 9am on Sunday.

It comes after masked demonstrators were seen at an anti-migrant protests in Portsmouth and Dover last weekend.

Daniel Thomas, also known as Danny Tommo, an activist who organised last weekend's protests, wrote on social media platform X that his group Patriot Platform would not attend the planned Portsmouth demonstration.

"No member, organiser, representative, or affiliate of Patriot Platform will attend, speak at, steward, or take part in any event in Portsmouth," he wrote.

Assistant Chief Constable Paul Bartolomeo said ahead of the planned marches: “It is important to stress that this power will apply to any groups that attend the protest and will be enforced equally and impartially.

“Let me be clear, these powers are not being implemented to prevent protest, but they are being used to help prevent crime and disorder, while making communities feel safer.

“We will support those who want to express their views peacefully and lawfully, but we will not tolerate those whose only aim is to create fear and incite violence.”

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has called on artificial intelligence companies to moderate the rate at which they advance model capabilities, proposing a three-step framework to pace development and create time to manage risks.

"We must slow the pace at which we improve the capabilities of AI models. Progress will still seem fast, and we must make wise use of the time we gain," Amodei said in an essay published on X.

His comments come after Anthropic published a threat intelligence report on Thursday revealing that various actors had used its Claude AI models for activities including weapons development, cyber operations, surveillance and fraud.

Worry over potential harm from AI deepened this week when Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned, stating that the "people building AI earnestly believe that it could kill us all by the end of the decade."

Amodei clarified that he was not advocating for a halt to model training or technical development, but rather ensuring companies take adequate time to align and secure their systems, alongside verification from third-party evaluators.

open image in gallery ( AFP/Getty )

As part of the proposed three-step strategy, Amodei suggested embedding permanent third-party reviewers within frontier AI companies, providing them with access to relevant tools and internal risk-assessment processes.

The wider sector has faced growing scrutiny over containment.

Reuters reported last week that a swarm of rogue OpenAI agents hijacked a German website, transforming it into a bulletin board for other AI agents. OpenAI officials kept the event under wraps while management dealt with the aftermath of a July breach of the open-source repository Hugging Face.

Multiple incidents in which AI agents from developers such as Anthropic rival OpenAI have breached or attempted to access external systems have intensified fears regarding model capacity and containment.

With a growing number of US lawmakers calling for new legislation to govern AI systems, Amodei said companies should voluntarily cooperate to establish standards.

News.title: Chelsea rescue draw as woeful defence punished by Hull
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and new manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

Chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

News.title: Bomb squad rescues rusty Red Roses
News.content:
England 48 Australia 15

England launched their WXV Global Series campaign with a second-half steamrollering of Australia in Salford.

A shock defeat looked a possibility after a ragged first half which saw the tenacious Wallaroos lead 10-5 at the break. It was the first time the Red Roses had trailed after 40 minutes for six years.

But a rusty England got their act together after the break in devastating fashion and ran in five tries in the space of 15 minutes to blow Australia away.

It is now 1,400 days since the Red Roses last lost a Test – the 2022 World Cup final against New Zealand.

The England power surge brought two line-out drive tries from hooker May Campbell, on her first Test start, and her replacement Bryony Field on her England debut, as coach John Mitchell unleashed a forward bomb squad from the bench.

In between, captain Meg Jones went over from a chip through by Holly Aitchison who was winning her 50th cap.

Mia Venner, Sadia Kabeya, Lucy Packer and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald went over for further tries to add to player of the match Abi Burton’s first half touchdown as the world champions turned it on for a crowd of 9,251 in the north-west and got the ball rolling in the 12-nation competition.

England face Canada at Exeter next Saturday in a repeat of last year’s World Cup final.

More to follow...

News.title: Lando Norris produces ‘best lap’ of his career to snatch Spanish GP pole
News.content:
Lando Norris said he had produced “one of the best laps” of his career as he snatched pole position from Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli by one hundredth of a second at the new Madring circuit in Madrid.

It had looked like being a straight fight between Mercedes and Ferrari for pole. Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who had earlier crashed heavily in practice, was fastest on his first run in Q3, edging out Antonelli by 0.061sec with Russell a further tenth or so back.

And if there was to be a surprise pole-sitter it looked most likely to be Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, who was fastest in Q2.

But Norris had other ideas. After Antonelli moved top with his final run in Q3, first Russell, who could only claim sixth, then Leclerc and then Hamilton failed to beat the Italian’s time. It looked for all the world as if Italy’s championship leader would be starting Sunday’s race from the front of the pack.

Norris, though, managed to produce what he described as “one of the best laps of my career”, setting the fastest time in the first sector and then impressively holding on until the end. The Briton’s pole lap was a whole second quicker than his best Q2 time. “Yes! Oh what a lap!” Norris screamed as he returned to the pits.

News.title: Jordan Cox looks a Joe Root clone as pair steer England home
News.content:
There is perhaps no batsman in Test history as accustomed as Joe Root to walking in with the scoreboard reading “not many for two” and his team in a tight spot.

That is where Root found himself once again soon after 11am on Saturday. His team were two for two, with both openers out for ducks, and the problems of the third evening bleeding into the fourth morning. A chaotic and patchwork Pakistan team suddenly believed Mohammad Abbas could inspire their defence of 130.

A familiar position for Root, sure, but not the young man at the other end, the rookie No 3 Jordan Cox. Together, they eased England out of a creeping crisis with such aplomb that the target was chased swiftly enough that the few thousand at Edgbaston were refunded 50 per cent of their ticket prices because so few overs were bowled. When Cox hit the winning run, a scrambled single into the off side, Root’s relief was palpable. His team had been tested, and he felt they would be “better for it”.

They had won his first series since returning to the captaincy 3-0, but not without a scare at the last. The scorecard will record this as a routine England eight-wicket win and, for the most part, it was. But England were rattled by Razaullah, a 21-year-old who spent the first two Tests of this series in Mardan, in the mountains of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa region near Pakistan’s border with Afghanistan. Having bowled quickly, he wreaked havoc on the third evening with his 63-ball 81, taking England from the brink of an innings victory to an awkward chase.

Razaullah’s partner with the bat was Abbas, who provided England with an almighty fright on the fourth morning. First ball, Ben Duckett was caught behind. The ball was angled in, demanding that it was played, then nipped slightly away, taking the edge. Duckett’s trudge off was glacial, with his curious Test summer over. He has scored England’s only century of the season, but failed to make fifty otherwise. In this series, he has averaged just eight.

News.title: Razaullah’s incredible hitting scrambles England’s minds
News.content:
England will look to complete the series whitewash as they hold a commanding position coming into day three of the third and final Test against Pakistan at Edgbaston in what could be the final day of the English Test summer.

England finished up their first innings on 453 on day two, with a mammoth 320-run lead over Pakistan. Five England batsmen passed the fifty mark; Emilio Gay, Harry Brook, Dan Lawrence, Jamie Smith and Ollie Robinson, but none went on to convert those half centuries into hundreds. It means that Ben Duckett’s century against New Zealand at Trent Bridge back in June will be the only England Test hundred of the summer, the first time that has happened in a six-Test summer. England managed 21 half centuries over the course of the summer, so it works out as 4.76% conversion rate.

Having seen England pile on the runs, Pakistan then lost a wicket with the first ball of their second innings, with Saim Ayub making a pair to sum up a miserable return to their Test side for the opener having been jettisoned in as part of wholesale changes for the visitors. Abdullah Shafique followed three balls later, with Robinson taking both wickets as his fine summer continued. Robinson now has 28 wickets across four Tests this summer at a staggering average of 7.75. Joe Root made history yesterday, taking his 220th catch, the most by an outfielder in Test history. Rain though prevented England the opportunity of potentially wrapping up a two-day finish in a Test in this country for the first time since 2000.

Pakistan will resume on 52/2, still 268 runs behind England, with Azan Awais resuming on 29 not out and will be joined by Shan Masood, who is on 21. Pakistan are yet to reach 200 or bat more than 51 overs in this series so the series whitewash may not be a million miles away. Will we see any rare Pakistan resistance in this series or will England’s seamers dominate again? Play on day three from Edgbaston is set to get under at 11am and it could be the final day of not just the series but the English Test summer.

News.title: Interest rates predicted to rise four times by July
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. Britain’s economy grew unexpectedly in July, handing Chancellor John Healey some breathing space ahead of the Budget.

The UK’s gross domestic product (GDP) expanded by 0.4pc during the month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS). Analysts had expected the UK economy to flatline.

Officials said pubs and clubs, advertisers and alcohol makers reported an increase in turnover linked to the World Cup, while many firms also said the second hottest July on record had a positive impact.

The data showed Britain’s economy may be benefitting from the massive investments in AI, with activity in telecoms expanding by 1.1pc in July, computer programming up 3.5pc and information services up 1.1pc.

The data will lend support to the “optimistic story” that John Healey tried to tell about the economy in a major speech this week.

Growth also accelerated from 0.3pc in June after Andy Burnham took over as Prime Minister in July.

It slightly eases pressure on the Chancellor after the cost of government borrowing costs rose to levels not seen in decades after a jump in the price of oil reignited a bond market sell-off.

The Treasury’s 10-year interest rate rose above 5.3pc on Thursday, a level not seen since 2007. It threatens to wipe around £10bn from Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom before his first Budget next month, according to economists at the Item Club. Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Badenoch must scrap triple lock, says senior Tory MP | Politician urges Conservatives to ‘slaughter some sacred cows’ to stabilise the public finances

2) | Michael O’Leary demands sacking of ‘incompetent’ air traffic control chief | Ryanair boss urges Transport Secretary to dismiss Martin Rolfe after IT meltdown grounds passengers

3) | Guardian staff threaten walkout over pay as paper hails record revenues | Journalists’ union will ballot members over strike in protest against company’s offer

4) | Hotel bosses criticise Burnham’s fresh assault on hospitality | Prime Minister gives mayors power for unlimited levy on stays in blow for pubs and families

5) | Iceland to become first British supermarket to open in Falklands | New shop will begin trading before Christmas despite rising tensions with Argentina over islands

What happened overnight

Oil prices remained at their highest level since May as tensions flared in the Middle East.

Brent crude was above $105 a barrel after after Iran-backed Houthis seized control of Yemen’s keyport of Mocha, threatening Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea.

Asian shares declined, tracking Wall Street losses. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 2.8pc to 63,442.30, while South Korea’s Kospi lost 2.3pc to 6,872.39.

Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dipped 0.8pc to 24,753.54. The Shanghai Composite index was down 1.8pc to 3,862.73.

Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 fell 1.2pc to 8,712.20.

Taiwan’s Taiex lost 1.7pc, while India’s Sensex declined 1pc.

On Thursday, Wall Street’s benchmark S&P 500 dropped 0.6pc in its fourth straight loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 0.6pc, and the technology-heavy Nasdaq composite fell 0.7pc.

Liverpool’s Swedish striker had a torrid time with injuries in his first season at Anfield, but the fit-again forward has started the season on fire with three goals in as many games. The quick-fire double from Isak (£6.0m) at Portman Road last time out were the only goals of the game as the Reds ran out 2–0 victors over Ipswich.



Resolute Tigers

Hull City have been the Premier League’s early surprise package, keeping three clean sheets in their opening fixtures, and amassing seven points over those games. TFF managers may be eyeing budget options: Konstantinos Tzolakis (£2.5m), Nobel Mendy (£2.5m), Semi Ajayi (£2.4m) and John Egan (£2.4m), but holding off until their trip to Stamford Bridge passes first before making an investment may be wise.



Thriller at the Emirates

While a 2-1 scoreline doesn’t scream ‘thriller’, there was a lot of enjoyable attacking play on display in the London derby. Three in-form players found the back of the net, with Kai Havertz (£5.1m), Martin Odegaard (£5.2m) and Morgan Rogers (£4.3m) all having started the season brightly.

News.title: Mainoo looks primed for battle with Man City’s new-look midfield
News.content:
This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Sports.title: Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich 3: Zian Flemming’s last-gasp winner seals consecutive wins for newly-promoted Tractor Boys
Sports.content:
ZIAN FLEMMING delivered a three-point harvest for Ipswich in South London as they beat Crystal Palace 3-2

Jorgen Strand Larsen looked to have saved Axel Disasi from disaster after his strike put Palace level following the Frenchman’s first-half sending off.



But there was to be no valiant comeback story for Palace as they fell to a defeat against Ipswich at Selhurst Park for the first time since 2010.

With identical records in the league it was no surprise there was nothing to separate these two sides in the opening half an hour, with goals from Anan Khalaili and Emersonn cancelling each other out.



But Disasi’s needless studs up challenge on Jack Clarke in the Ipswich half saw Palace surrender the lead and a chance at successive wins in the Premier League, something they have not done since last December.

Leif Davis had been the provider for the Tractor Boys opener before he turned goalscorer for the goal that put Gary O’Neil’s side on course for their first win in the league since the opening day,



Yet a profligate Ipswich display in the second half gave the Eagles enough of a lift to get back into the game despite being down to 10-men, with Strand Larsen’s clinical strike across goal seeing the two sides level entering the 89th minute.

But a Davis header floated towards goal and hit the crossbar before it fell kindly to Flemming, whose shot wrong-footed Benitez to squirm in at the far post and see Ipswich take the three points.

Palace boss Pierre Sage was without Dean Henderson because of an ankle injury he picked up in their Conference League final win against Freiburg.

That saw Sage opt for Walter Benitez between the sticks, marking his first Premier League start since March, while Adam Wharton wore the captain’s armband in Henderson’s place.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The South Londoners were also without their famous Holmesdale Fanatics ultras, the Ipswich clash being the second league game without the group after they effectively disbanded.

But they could have desperately used their voices in support after Disasi’s silly red card – and perhaps an even more damning assessment when the away end started chanting “you’re support is f***ing s***.”

The balance of the clash had been on a knife-edge in the opening quarter of an hour, with neither team able to force a breakthrough.

That was until Yeremy Pino cut through the Ipswich defence like butter to play in Daichi Kamada, who in turn passed the ball to flying right wing-back Khalail who thundered home his first goal for the Eagles.

Palace threatened to grab a second when Jorgen Strand Larsen, fresh off the back of his brace against Middlesbrough midweek, lashed the ball at goal after a great ball in behind by Khalaili.



But his effort went straight at Kjell Scherpen, who parried it away with firm hands.

Ipswich got themselves level pegging again after Emersonn was left unchallenged by the Palace backline, who fell asleep waiting for an offside flag that never arrived.

Emersonn notched his second goal of the season as he headed a wonderful Davis cross past the hapless Benitez 10 minutes after the opener.

Another 10 minutes later, Disasi inexplicably decided he simply had to challenge Clarke – making his first start of the season for the visitors – for a loose ball.

But the 28-year-old was late to the challenge, and was promptly given his marching orders by Chris Kavanagh before VAR Craig Pawson confirmed the decision – with the former Chelsea man standing by the corner flag in front of the players tunnel while he bizarrely waited for confirmation on the stonewall red card.



Sage opted for the conservative approach and switched out Pino for Takehiro Tomiyasu.

And the signs of a goal were there to see when only a poor touch stopped Clarke from shooting from close range, with the ball cleared by Chris Richards.

The breakthrough would come a minute later, with Abdul Fatawu slipping a pass down the side of the Eagles defence for Dara O’Shea, who delivered a ball into Emersonn whose failed attempt at a shot then found Davis in acres of space at the far post.

Ipswich seemed to play with their food for much of the second half, with one occasion seeing Julio Enciso speed in behind Richards to lay a pass to Fatawu who then tried to turn in the area instead of shooting before Palace got back in numbers to defend.

Benitez then produced a smart save to deny Clarke, but it wasn’t until the 68th minute when winds of change in the game started to open the door for a Palace equaliser.



Palace continued to threaten as attack after attack swooped towards the Ipswich box, before Strand Larsen sunk his talons into the goal with his vicious shot across goal.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The home fans had also found their voice even without their ultras, drowning out the away support for the final 20 minutes and that was reflected on the pitch with it seeming like it was the visitors who were a man down.

But Flemming’s first Prem goal of the season saw Ipswich escape potential embarrassment by landing all three points.

Sports.title: Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2: Kevin Schade nets brace to secure point in four-goal thriller as Bees maintain unbeaten start
Sports.content:
MARCO ROSE’S Bournemouth crashed landed against their bogey side Brentford before flying into Europe.

The German had to watch in agony again as his wasteful side threw away a lead for the fourth Premier League game in a row.



But the Bees weren’t complaining thanks to two-goal marksman Kevin Schade who gobbled up two gifts from the hosts.

Brentford are now 12 league games unbeaten against the south coast club, who can have no complaints they’ve flopped again against the Londoners.



And Rose will be scratching his head wondering why he is still waiting for his first Premier League win.

Bees defender Keane Lewis-Potter curled a handsome shot just wide of Dorde Petrovic’s far post after just three minutes.

But Bournemouth slowly got more possession and five minutes later had their first chance – one that should have been taken.

Marcus Tavernier set-up Antonio Silva with a perfect free-kick just eight yards out but the Portuguese defender headed down and wide.

And that miss backfired on the hosts on 35 minutes when they gifted the opening goal to the visitors.

Adrien Truffert lost possession to Mamadou Sangare. He fed Yehor Yarmoliuk who crossed for Schade to head home off Petrovic’s fingers and the post.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

That was the first time this season that Bournemouth had failed to score first in their four Prem games.

And to their credit they responded in style and should have equalised through their Brazilian striker Rayan two minutes later.

Justin Kluivert’s angled drive was pushed out by Bees goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher to Rayan, who blazed over the bar from 10 yards.

But it wasn’t long before the Cherries levelled on 38 minutes and once again it was Kluivert who was making his mark in the box.

Rayan did well to find Evanilson who set-up the Dutchman, who turned well and fired into the far corner.



Kluivert was in red-hot form and three minutes after the break, his drive was tipped over the bar by Kelleher.

And Silva was cursing his luck from Kluivert’s resulting corner when he headed the ball wide again.

But then Alex Scott suffered in front of goal when he burst clear onto Evanilson’s pass and somehow managed to slice his shot horribly wide.



The home faithful couldn’t quite believe what they were watching knowing that the Bees had the Indian sign over them.

Marcus Tavernier calmed the nerves when he drove home Evanilson’s pass on 52 minutes to put the Cherries ahead.

But Bournemouth cannot hang on to leads these days and they stupidly gifted the visitors their second goal three minutes later.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Petrovic, under no pressure, senselessly passed the ball straight to Schade who only had to lob the ball over the embarrassed keeper into the net.

The Bees’ luck continued into stoppage time when Cherries substitute Ben Gannon-Doak saw his shot deflected onto the post.

Sports.title: Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2: Igor Jesus’ last-gasp winner ensures Emery’s woeful start to season continues
Sports.content:
IGOR JESUS made sure that Unai Emery STILL cannot get the better Oliver Glasner.

And record signing Liam Delap provided the platform for Nottingham Forest’s victory when he powered home his first goal since making the £50million summer move from Chelsea.



But the result meant the Spaniard has now failed to beat the Austrian coach in EIGHT games – seven of them when Glasner was in charge at Nottingham Forest.

Sub Jesus struck with two minutes left to condemn the Villa boss to their third defeat of the season – after a winless league start for Emery.



Emery’s only consolation came when Brazilian sub Alysson headed a second half equaliser for his first Villa goal since a January move from Gremio.

It also broke Villa’s duck in the Premier League on a day when Emery gave some of his new signings the chance to shine.

But it was Delap who opened the scoring less than 50 seconds into the second half with a 25 yard drive.

Forest kept the pressure on Villa despite Alysson’s goal – and Jesus, who had only come on 12 minutes earlier, was on the end of Daniel Munoz’s cross to make sure of their first win of the season.



It must have left Emery wondering what more he has to do to overcome the curse of Glasner.

But he will also be concerned that his new-look Villa side has still to gel four games into the season.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

As for Glasner, his carefully assembled Forest squad are starting to click after the disappointment of being denied victory against Tottenham last week by VAR.

Glasner was forced into a late re-think after losing two defenders to injury just 124 hours before the game.

Jair Cunha and Nikola Milenkovic were both ruled out on Friday afternoon although both players travelled to Villa Park.



It meant Glasner switching Ola Aina into the centre of defence with Munoz making his full Forest debut as a wing-back.

Villa will wonder how they did not open the scoring after seven minutes as keeper Matz Sels pulled off a huge save to deny Victor Lindelhof.

Emi Buendia’s cross hit Lindelhof and wrong-footed Sels who saved with his feet and stretched out to scoop off the line.

The ball then hit Forest defender Murillo and bounced against the post.

Glasner’s men responded with James McAtee then Morgan Gibbs-White testing Villa keeper Zion Suzuki.



But Emery then suffered an injury blow as Pau Torres limped off – and was replaced by Tyrone Mings.

Nicolas Jackson picked up a yellow card for a shove off the ball on defender Ousmane Diomande.

But Forest could have taken the lead just before half-time when Neco Williams sent his shot over the bar.

Emery decided changes were needed and Jackson was hooked at the break with Tammy Abraham and wide man Alysson coming on for a unusually below par George Hemmings.

Any hopes the Villa boss had of switching the game in his side’s favour disappeared straight after the break though.



Bouba Kamara’s attempted flick was pounced on by Delap who announced his Forest arrival in style.

It was his first goal since January when he scored in Chelsea’s defeat at Fulham.

And Delap was clearly win the mood for more goals as he headed into the side netting after an hour.

He looked to have smashed home his second goal, but it was ruled offside much to Villa’s relief.

Emery had already introduced two new summer signings from the bench – with Switzerland midfielder Johan Manzambi and ex-PSG teenager Ibrahim Mbaye coming on after 63 minutes.



Mbaye brought save out of Sels – and Villa levelled from the resulting corner.

Skipper John McGinn produced a pinpoint cross for Alysson to head from from eight yards.

But Forest still sensed victory and summer signing Xaver Schlager brought a full stretch save from Suzuki.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They continued to push for a second goal – and they deservedly found the net late on.

Jesus was presented with an opening six yards from goal – and he gratefully accepted.

Sports.title: Chelsea 2 Hull 2: Pedro on fire as Blues’ new-look attack still lethal as ever but Xabi Alonso’s defensive woes exposed
Sports.content:
There really is never a dull moment at Chelsea, on or off the field.

At the end of a week when their boardroom power struggle moved towards resolution, manager Xabi Alonso is no closer to sorting out the balance of his chaotic team.



And football is all the better for it, with Hull playing a full part in another thriller.

The Blues score for fun but cannot defend for toffee.



Their tricky trio combined to great effect again, with Joao Pedro teeing up Morgan Rogers for their first goal and Cole Palmer crossing for Pedro to make it 2-2.

But in between, Chelsea showed the same vulnerability playing in a new-look back four as they had with three central defenders.



An error by Jorrel Hato gifted Mo Belloumi his first goal, and a rush of blood to the head by goalkeeper Emi Martinez led to the Algerian’s second as Sergej Jakirovic’s side stunned Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea have not kept a clean sheet in the Premier League since January, a run of 20 games with three different goalkeepers.

Both sides had chances to claim victory. Neither could take them, but neutrals were once more the winners.

From start to finish, this was Chelsea’s latest attempt to bring back the glory days of the Barclays.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

True, the eighth minute was the longest their fans had had to wait for a goal so far in the Premier League.

But when Rogers continued his own fast start to life at a new club, hopes were high.

The Blues survived a dangerous corner and the front three moved the ball across the field, from Palmer to Pedro to Rogers.

The England star surged past Regan Slater with ease and hit a firm left-footed shot past the badly-positioned Konstantinos Tzolakis and inside the near post.

It was the first time Hull had conceded in the league and a second looked to be in the post.



John Egan had to cut out a Malo Gusto cross, then Tzolakis saved from Pedro Neto.

Chelsea’s set pieces, orchestrated theatrically by Austin MacPhee from the technical area, were also causing the visitors some problems.

But then Hull equalised out of absolutely nothing.



A long ball down the left flank was just about collected by full back Ryan Giles. As his slow, high cross looped into the penalty area, Giles must have been tempted to start running back to his own half.

But Hato watched the ball bounce and then go over his head to where Belloumi was waiting to crash home a first-time effort.

The visiting fans had already been in good voice and good humour. Moments later, there was bedlam in their section of the Shed End.

Another ball in from the left fell to captain Lewie Coyle, whose low shot was deflected behind by Levi Colwill’s block.

From the resulting corner, Martinez made an ill-judged charge from his line. Semi Ajayi easily beat him to it, only for his header to come back off the bar.



But McBurnie reacted quickest and laid the ball back into Belloumi’s path. The Algerian’s shot took a deflection – it seemed off the hapless Hato – and nestled in the net.

Chants of “We are top of the league” were soon followed by “We’re gonna win the league”.

The sun was out, it was still September, so why not?

Jakirovic was furious when Tzolakis was almost guilty of another error leading to a goal, when he allowed Pedro to charge down his attempted clearance.



Belloumi blocked a Gusto shot to send Hull into the break ahead.

Alonso had to act after his latest experiment had failed and it was no surprise to see Hato replaced by Pep Chavarria.

The home team took charge and the visitors were having to resort to some pretty agricultural challenges.

The Duke of Wellington famously said of his troops: “I don’t know what effect these men will have upon the enemy, but, by God, they frighten me.”



Hull’s big strapping lads will have a similar impact on many teams.

Egan and Matt Crooks were booked for full-blooded fouls on Chavarria and Rogers respectively, either side of Reece James trying to catch out Tzolakis again at his near post with a free kick.

Then Palmer stood up a cross to the back post where Nobel Mendy stopped Pedro converting and came off worst in the clash of heads, which forced him off.

Back came Hull. Martinez spilled a less-than-fearsome shot by Slater but recovered to stop McBurnie putting in the rebound.



Sorba Thomas, barely a day after rolling his Range Rover on the way to training, came on as part of a double winger change, and immediately looked lively.

But then Chelsea equalised. Palmer crossed from the left for Pedro, who rifled home to set up the last 25 minutes of the game perfectly.

The home team were clear favourites to find a winner.

Ajayi eased Gusto off the ball, Tzolakis saved from James and Palmer rejected the chance for a first-time shot with his right foot, only for one with his left to be blocked.



As the clock ticked down, Tzolakis saved from Rogers.

Then Stamford Bridge held its breath as a Giles cross was met by substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho, only for Martinez to make a good stop.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The football gods – and timekeepers – offered up six minutes of added time.

There were close things, and the drama was not over until Palmer sent a free kick well over the bar with the last kick of the game.

Sports.title: Liverpool 0 Fulham 0: Iraola left pulling his hair out as Reds’ £400million attack look sluggish and sloppy
Sports.content:
ANDONI IRAOLA was left pulling his hair out over a no-show from Bradley Barcola and the rest of Liverpool’s near- £400M attackers.

The Frenchman, striker Alexander Isak, playmaker Florian Wirtz and Victor Munoz all but stank out Anfield.



The clash offered Fulham’s under-fire boss Alvaro Arbeloa some much–needed breathing space – indeed his side could and should have won.

But after Liverpool’s fourth successive Premier League draw at home for the first time in 15 years it was Iraola who was really feeling the strain.



Since replacing Arne Slot in the summer he has now overseen three league draws – his only slice of domestic joy a 2–0 win over newly-promoted Ipswich Town.

That quartet of Barcola, Isak, Wirtz and Munoz might look good on paper but they looked nothing like it as Arbeloa’s players delivered a point that before kick–off few, if any, expected them to leave with.

Iraola had demanded a start fast after his side had gone behind early in three of their first four games under him.

He didn’t get the response he wanted.

Other than a dart into the Cottagers’ box by Alexander Isak of Bradley Barcola’s clever through-ball, Liverpool were sluggish from kick–off and almost criminally sloppy.

Alisson didn’t look like one of the best goalkeepers in the world at all with a mad short pass in his box directed at Ryan Gravenberch.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Josh King, at the start of a performance that underlined why he is seen as his club’s most talented academy graduate in a generation, pounced as Alisson crashed into him.

Gonzalo Garcia found the ball at his feet a dozen yards out and had the width of the goal to aim at but slightly scuffed his shot straight at Jeremy Jacquet on the line.

Worse for the visitors, they should have had a penalty for Liverpool’s no1 caught King without question as he went for the ball but referee Thomas Bramall didn’t spot the offence.

Astonishingly, VAR Tony Harrington reviewed and ignored what looked like a clear spot kick.

Fulham hardly looked like a side looking for their first win of the season with new boss Alvaro Arbeola, once of Anfield’s parish, going into the clash under a cloud having lost his first three Prem games since replacing Marco Silva.



But if he was expecting all-out pressure from his fellow Spaniard’s side, it didn’t happen.

Only Munoz, the cheapest of that so–called star attack at £34M and also the smallest of the lot of them, did force a brilliant parry from Bernd Leno with a header off Dominik Szoboszlai’s corner.

Yet Liverpool’s first-half performance, after the power and glory of the midweek 2 – 1 comeback win over Atletico Madrid wasn’t even average as frustration festered in the Kop.



Iraola was equally unimpressed, replacing Kostas Tsimikas with Milos Kerkez straight after the break then Ryan Gravenberch and Munoz for Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo.

The three subbed off had all been brought in for what at the start would have been seen as an easy three points yet it only turned into a slog with Fulham looking so much more together.

Isak, with three Prem goals already this campaign and finally looking like he was worth £130M was more of a spectator than a striker.



Winger Barcola, at £123M from Paris Saint-Germain and a double Champions League winner, was hooked for Rio Ngumoha.

His most important contribution before his 72nd minute exit had been heading clear to give Fulham a corner.

Wirtz, again, wandered through a game, never showing anything like the kind of quality that brought him to Anfield from the Bundesliga for £100M.



Mac Allister, scorer of the scorching winner in the midweek Champions League victory did make a near- immediate impact.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

His clever touch found Szoboszlai but the Hungarian’s drive was straight at Leno – not so at the other end after Arbeloa’s side had played their way through Liverpool’s midfield.

King let fly from 20 yards but his fine 76th minute effort was dealt with in kind as Alisson desperately pushed wide.

Sports.title: Liverpool's £400m attack draws a blank in frustrating Fulham stalemate - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Liverpool's £400m attack draws a blank in frustrating Fulham stalemate - 5 talking points

LIVERPOOL 0-0 FULHAM: Andoni Iraola fielded Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Victor Munoz in attack, but the pricey foursome struggled to break down the away side

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola summed up Liverpool's lack of cutting edge (Image: James Gill/Getty Images)

Liverpool's expensively-assembled attack failed to click into gear as Fulham claimed their first point of the Premier League season in a stalemate at Anfield.

‌



Andoni Iraola started with a front four worth £398.5million, in the form of Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola, Florian Wirtz and Victor Munoz, but they did not play up to their cumulative price tag as Liverpool recorded their fourth straight draw in the Premier League at Anfield - their longest such winless stretch at home for five and a half years.

‌



Fulham should have taken the lead when Alisson made a mess of a pass out to Ryan Gravenberch, but Jeremy Jacquet cleared Gonzalo Garcia's shot off the line. Munoz then forced a strong save from Bernd Leno with a header from a corner as Liverpool threatened.

‌



Dominik Szoboszlai shot straight at Leno as Liverpool failed to build up any sort of momentum, despite Iraola ringing the changes after the break. Josh King tested Alisson with an effort from the edge of the box before Rodrigo Muniz's poor touch spurned another opening for the away side.

There was no grandstand finish as a subdued Anfield crowd went home frustrated, with Isak flicking a late header wide from a corner. Here are the talking points.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Ropey Reds

Liverpool's defence has looked vulnerable this season and there was a nervy start at Anfield against Fulham. Alisson held his hands up after they got away with conceding early on, but Iraola should be worried by fact the experienced goalkeeper is making blunders.

Alisson's pass to Gravenberch was a terrible decision and the Brazil international was also fortunate that Josh King decided to hurdle his rash challenge inside the box, rather than accept the contact and earn a penalty. Alisson was indebted to Jacquet, who retreated to the line to clear Garcia's effort.

‌



View 4 Images Alisson was fortunate to get away with an early blunder (Image: Getty Images)

Wirtz needs to step up

Florian Wirtz has a huge weight on his shoulders for Liverpool, as the fulcrum of their creativity in attack. The German never shies away from his responsibilities, but his output is still some way off what the club expected when they paid Bayer Leverkusen £116.5million last summer.

His tally of seven goals for Liverpool is well short of where it should be and the way he dragged an effort wide from the edge of the box in the first half showed what needs to be improved.

‌



View 4 Images Florian Wirtz's goal output is poor for Liverpool (Image: James Gill/Getty Images)

Not happening for Barcola

Liverpool's £123m summer signing missed two great chances to get his first goal for the club against Atletico Madrid in mid-week before leaving the pitch with cramp. Iraola has called for patience, citing the Frenchman's minimal pre-season, and his sharpness is definitely still lacking.

Timothy Castagne did well to block a back-post volley from Barcola in the first half, but his effort was going nowhere near the goal. In the second half, he got to the byline, but his cutback was easily cleared. Barcola was then taken off in the 72nd minute, having shown very little.

‌



View 4 Images Bradley Barcola was ineffective once more (Image: James Gill/Getty Images)

Fulham on the board

Alvaro Arbeloa arrived at his former stomping ground under pressure following a poor start to the season. Defeats by Chelsea, Sunderland and Crystal Palace had left the Cottagers without a point from their opening three games, despite four goals scored and some encouraging play.

Arbeloa will be happy with much of his side's play at Anfield, with Fulham limiting Liverpool to few chances. But having scored twice against Chelsea and Palace, they couldn't produce the bit of magic they needed to grab all three points.

‌



No impact off the bench

Iraola brought on Milos Kerkez for Kostas Tsimikas at half-time before introducing Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister, Jeremie Frimpong and Rio Ngumoha. But there was to be no late winner, with Leno relatively untroubled in the Fulham goal as the game petered out.

Anfield is supposed to be a fortress for the Reds but at the moment it is far too easily breached.

Sports.title: 'I could barely afford food on £300-a-week at Celtic and was miserable – but I became club icon'
Sports.content:
Stiliyan Petrov says he struggled to afford his weekly shop on a measly £300-a-week wage at Celtic despite signing for £2.8million. The Bulgarian midfielder joined for a hefty fee but struggled during his first few months in Scotland before Martin O'Neill helped him turn a corner.

Petrov joined the Hoops from CSKA Sofia in 1999, agreeing a deal for just under £3m – which was an enormous fee at the time. However, the ex-Aston Villa star admitted his initial time at Celtic was full of financial issues that weren't fixed until O'Neill arrived one year later.

During an appearance on the All Out Football podcast with Laura Kirk-Francis and Gabby Agbonlahor, the 47-year-old revealed his struggles after joining the Scottish giants. When questioned on his wages compared to his signing fee, Petrov said: "Listen, at that time the money wasn't important for me. I was naive to move. It wasn't about the money for me. It was never about the money.

You can listen to brand new episodes of In The Mixer on Spotify and Apple Podcasts!

‌



Celtic and Rangers hit with stadium bans after ugly scenes in Old Firm clash READ MORE :

BBC football pundit breached editorial standards as he apologises after investigation launches READ MORE :

"Listen I could have left Celtic, I could have left Villa for a lot more money in different destinations. It was never about the money. It was about what you want to leave behind you. I've played for two great clubs. I've played with some incredible players and I won't change it."

Petrov's luck changed when O'Neill arrived, as he also struggled with fitting in as part of the team. When asked when his pay changed, he explained: "Six months after, Martin O'Neill took over. Obviously, I was celebrating John Barnes being sacked because I wasn't playing.

"I had a really difficult time. John never really put in any effort to help. I had a really difficult time for the first six months. Forget about bill issues, financial issues, forget about that. But the language barrier was a big problem for me because the dressing room was pushing me away. I wasn't talking to anyone. I wasn't communicating.

‌



"Go to training, get changed, train back home. That was me for six months. I was trying, I was thinking how can I fit in? But you know when you're not in a conversation, when you don't know the people's problem, and I could see they were pushing me away.

"But then the change happened. John Barnes got sacked and Martin took over. He gave me six weeks to get fit and show him that I can play on that team. I had a really good pre-season and had to lose 10 kilos as well. That was a lot in the pre-season. All that not eating and training twice a day."

Highlighting the Celtic manager's handling of his "dodgy agent," Petrov added: "When he [O'Neill] was happy with the pre-season, with everything I've done, he called me and he went, 'I've looked at your contract. I'm giving you more money.'

"So I try to explain about the agent. He said, 'Forget about the agent. Forget about the agent. This I will offer you, are you happy [with it]?' So I went from £300-a-week to £2,500-a-week."

‌



View 2 Images Petrov eventually found his footing at Celtic (Image: Stu Forster/ALLSPORT)

Petrov also recounted a time when his family visited from Bulgaria, and he had to wait for a game bonus to arrive in order to restock his fridge. Explaining how his family weren't aware of his situation, the ex-midfielder added: "The day [his family visited] I was expecting a bonus, a game bonus. So the day they landed in Scotland, I had about £65.

"I couldn't even do the shopping. I just couldn't face them. They never knew my issues, my problems. I wasn't ready to share that."

Petrov's luck eventually changed and he became a prolific figure in the early 2000s for Celtic. He won 10 trophies in Scotland, including four league titles and also reached the UEFA Cup final - now known as the Europa League - in the 2002/03 season.

‌



After spending seven seasons at Villa, Petrov retired in 2013 following an acute leukaemia diagnosis the year prior. The ex-midfielder did return to training in 2016 after recovering from the illness but never returned to the professional game.

Sports.title: Richarlison digs out Tottenham in new statement after seeing dream transfer collapse
Sports.content:
Richarlison digs out Tottenham in new statement after seeing dream transfer collapse

Tottenham forward Richarlison has spoken out on the collapse of his proposed loan move to Brazilian club Vasco da Gama, pointing the finger at Spurs for reaching their loan limit

View 2 Images Richarlison has taken aim at Tottenham Hotspur after his move to Vasco da Gama fell through (Image: (Photo by Shaun Brooks - CameraSport via Getty Images))

Tottenham Hotspur striker Richarlison has taken aim at Spurs following the collapse of his proposed transfer to Vasco da Gama. Spurs reached an agreement with the Brazilian side for the 29-year-old, with Vasco da Gama failing to settle personal terms.

‌



Yet the player has taken to social media to lay the blame at Tottenham's door, claiming they were responsible for hitting their loan quota, preventing what would have been a dream transfer to his homeland. Speaking on Instagram, translated via geGlobo, the Brazilian said: "Hey there, Vasco fans. This week has been pretty hectic. I decided to take some time to thank the Vasco fans. Pedrinho, Felipe.

‌



"We were very close to me signing with Vasco. My team, the team of my whole family.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"It was a close call. I had made it very clear to Pedrinho and Felipe from the beginning of the conversation that I wanted to play for Vasco until December. When other clubs and other offers came up, I made it clear that they were my priority."

"This time, it was a close call. Unfortunately, Tottenham reached the loan limit, so it didn't work out either. But that's it. I wanted to thank you, the Vasco fans, who sent many kind messages.

‌



"Asking what time and day I would be at the airport so they could come and have a party and pick me up. But let's leave that for another time. I believe I'll be at São Januário, in Barreira, soon.

"You know how much I care about you all, and one day I will realize this dream, which is mine, my grandfather's, and my family's. I'm speaking from the heart because I really want to be at Vasco. That's it. Thank you all very much.

"Soon we will be wearing the Vasco shirt. There's even one over there, there are many over there. I found this one, and since Pedrinho has been at Vasco, in charge, he sends me many Vasco shirts, at every launch, he knows I'm a Vasco fan. Thanks. Soon we will be at São Januário, in Barreira, and 'that's us.'"

‌



View 2 Images Richarlison also saw a move to Everton collapse (Image: Marc Atkins, Getty Images)

Richarlison has been trying to force through a move away from the club after being left out of Roberto De Zerbi's 25-man Premier League squad.

The Brazilian had been angling for a way out before the British transfer window shut on September 1, with previous club Everton exploring a nostalgic return, but that move collapsed at the last moment.

‌



Trabzonspor also attempted to land his services, submitting bids of £15million and £20m, but a switch failed to materialise.

Richarlison participated in the first team's warm-up session on Thursday, though his exclusion from the Premier League squad means he is unable to play until January at the earliest.

Sports.title: Premier League clubs 'raise concerns' over new laws introduced this season
Sports.content:
Premier League clubs 'raise concerns' over new laws introduced this season

Premier League bosses have introduced a number of changes this season, with an eye on increasing how long the ball is in play and reducing overall match length

View 2 Images If a player receives treatment, they must leave the pitch for 60 seconds

Aston Villa are said to be among the Premier League clubs to raise concerns about new rules around injuries and substitutions.

‌



In a change introduced for the start of the 2026/27 season, players who have received medical attention must leave the pitch and wait 60 seconds before they return.

‌



This leaves affected teams down to 10 men for at least a minute, until they are waved back on following a break in play.

‌



Similarly, if a player takes longer than 10 seconds to leave the field after they have been substituted, their replacement has to wait for the first break in play after a minute before they are able to come on.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Premier League bosses are happy with the implementation of the new laws, meaning match lengths have been reduced by three minutes and playing time increased by the same amount.

But the Daily Mail reports that some top-flight teams, including Villa have reached out to Pro Ref regarding the use of the new rules.

The general sentiment is that referees are not using 'sufficient judgement' to determine when a player is genuinely injured and when one is intentionally trying to waste time.

‌



Decreasing delays within a match and increasing the amount of time the ball is in play has been an area of focus for decision makers. As well as new rules regarding injuries and subs, there are also timers in place to take goal kicks and throw-ins, all designed to speed up the game.

View 2 Images Referees have been tasked with reducing time-wasting during matches

Earlier this week, the Premier League issued an update on the effectiveness of the new initiatives.

‌



The statement reads: “New Laws of the Game, introduced at the start of this season, aimed at managing momentum and reducing delaying tactics are already showing a positive impact on effective playing time in the Premier League.

“Up to Match Round 3, the average match length stands at 97min 48secs – compared with 100:45 at the same point last season, while effective playing time has increased to 57:13 from 54:19 when comparing the first three match rounds.

“This shows an increase in the ball-in-play ratio from 53.9 per cent up to 58.5 per cent so far this season.”

Sports.title: New twist for Mason Greenwood as Fenerbahce issue blunt statement after manager resignation
Sports.content:
New twist for Mason Greenwood as Fenerbahce issue blunt statement after manager resignation

The managerial drama at Fenerbahce has thrown Mason Greenwood's new club into chaos

View 3 Images Mason Greenwood has endured a turbulent time at his new club (Image: 2026 UEFA)

There's been yet another twist in the management drama at Fenerbahce. Mason Greenwood's new club have released a statement insisting that head coach Ismail Kartal is "still in his position."

‌



The update came late on Friday, just 24 hours after Kartal publicly resigned following his side's 1-1 Champions League draw with Roma. Former Manchester United forward Greenwood, 24, has endured a turbulent time since moving to the club from Marseille this summer, due to the club's poor form and subsequent saga involving Kartal.

‌



The drama ignited as Kartal announced in his post-match press conference after the Roma tie that he was to leave his post. However, Fenerbahce president Aziz Yildirim refused to sanction Kartal's departure.

‌



Yildirim said in a statement released on Fenerbahce's website: "Ismail Kartal is still in charge. The club should support our coach. Until I leave, Ismail Kartal is the head coach of Fenerbahce."

That stance has since been reiterated with a blunt communication posted on Friday. The club said: "Our Head Coach, Mr. İsmail Kartal, is still in his position.

Baffled Champions League star learns his manager resigned straight after final whistle READ MORE :

Fenerbahce manager resigns from fourth stint hours after Mason Greenwood decision READ MORE :

"Our team will continue preparations for the Gaziantep FK match with a training session tomorrow at 11.30am under the direction of our Head Coach İsmail Kartal. We hereby inform the public."

‌



Kartal only returned to Fenerbahce for his fourth spell as manager this summer. Speaking to the media following the club's midweek Champions League clash, the 65-year-old said: "I am resigning from my position while there is still time. I am resigning with the understanding that I will never return.

"I have been here for three months. From the beginning of the season until today, the training sessions and camps I conducted with my players … our president and managers tried to help us in every way.

View 3 Images Fenerbahce head coach Ismail Kartal speaks during a press conference following the UEFA Champions League tie against Roma (Image: 2026 Anadolu)

‌



"Those were wonderful days. As of this evening, I congratulate my players, and I am resigning from my position. Therefore, I would like to thank all my fans, media members, staff, and fellow players who have supported me until today. I made this decision to pave the way for my club. We made this decision together as a team."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Kartal won the Turkish Super Cup during his first spell in charge in 2014, while as a player he won two league titles with the club. However, Fenerbahce have struggled so far this season.

‌



They currently sit ninth in the Turkish top-flight. President Yildirim slammed the attitude of the club's fans and the media for putting "pressure" on Kartal.

At his press conference, the manager alluded to the criticism, noting that he was hit with a water bottle from the stands during the Roma game. His shock announcement sent shockwaves through the club.

View 3 Images Fenerbahce Sports Club President Aziz Yildirim has had his say on Kartal (Image: Bunyamin Celik/Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



English full-back Archie Brown was taken by surprise when told of his manager's resignation after the Roma game. Quizzed whether Kartal had told his players that he was resigning from the team, Brown seemed puzzled.

He was then informed that his manager had quit in the post-match conference, prompting Brown to say: "As coach? He’s not the coach any more? I didn't know about this."

The impending change of management comes just two months of Greenwood's signing. Fenerbahce paid Marseille around £33million for the one-time England international, with United receiving £13million. Greenwood has featured 11 times so far. He has scored four goals and registered three assists.

Sports.title: Hollie Doyle blog: Big fan of Forty Years On in Sceptre Stakes
Sports.content:
Sky Sports Racing ambassador Hollie Doyle previews the final day of the St Leger Festival at Doncaster - live on Sky Sports Racing – alongside top-quality action on Champions’ Weekend at The Curragh.

Scott filly can make winning Stakes debut

I've made no secret of my admiration for FORTY YEARS ON who can make an instant impact in Pattern company when she contests the feature race at Doncaster on Sunday, the Japan Racing Association Sceptre Fillies Stakes (3.05).

George Scott, who won Friday's Doncaster Cup with Caballo De Mar, has found a great opportunity for this most progressive daughter of Mayson who was much too good for her rivals in a valuable handicap at Goodwood last month.

She enjoys ease underfoot and can win for the sixth time in eight starts at the possible expense of Shadwell's Touleen, who brings solid Group One form to the race after her luckless run in the Coronation Stakes at Royal Ascot.

She did look a bit awkward in the Valiant Stakes last time so the cheekpieces may just sharpen her focus, while Planet Seeker looks over-priced on the strength of her York form and her creditable fourth in the Group 3 Oak Tree Stakes at The Goodwood Festival.

Longer trip ideal for Bailey gelding in Mallard

It's hard to fault SAY WHAT YOU SEE in the Betfred Mallard Handicap (3.40) on Sunday following a string of rock-solid races for his trainer Liam Bailey this year.

He built on a near miss at Southwell with an eye-catching run at York's Ebor Festival, staying on from a long way back to finish a closing third over 12 furlongs and should appreciate this longer trip.

There's probably a nice race in Godolphin's Valedictory who was a little one-paced over two miles at York last time, having looked the real deal earlier in the season with back-to-back wins at Goodwood and Newmarket. He has something to prove off his current mark, however.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Doyle bit back at Sky Sports Racing's Seb Sanders after criticism of his winning ride in the Flying Childers at Doncaster, which saw Final Objective veer across the track and cause a rival to stumble badly

Boughey has strong hand in sprint

I like George Boughey's lightly raced ASUKA in the Betfred 'The Classic Bookmaker' Handicap (1.55) on Sunday's Doncaster card.

Dropping back to six furlongs on such a big galloping track shouldn't be an issue for the Night Of Thunder gelding who confirmed himself in top form over further at Chester last time when a poor draw and an interrupted run put paid to his chances.

George has a strong hand in the race with stable mate Oliver Show also bringing some strong form to the table. His run behind subsequent winner Inspired at Goodwood last time reads well and the first-time visor is an interesting angle.

Easier surface a positive for course winner

I'm looking forward to seeing LANGSTONE back on an easier surface in the Betfred City Of Doncaster Handicap (2.30) on Sunday.

Clive Cox's three-year-old broke his maiden over course and distance in the spring before following up on the All-Weather but didn't enjoy the fast ground in the Britannia at Royal Ascot. He hasn't been seen in public since so he arrives on Town Moor much fresher than his rivals and remains well treated off a slightly reduced mark of 92.

Zooming should also appreciate a more sympathetic surface for the first time since winning her maiden at Newmarket last autumn. She has been highly tried this year and drops into handicap company for the first time off what looks a workable mark of 94.

Image: The Sceptre Stakes headlines the final day at Doncaster as the fabulous four-day festival draws to a close

Goddess can have her day in the sun

I can't wait to see how SUN GODDESS performs back at Group One level in the Moyglare Stud Stakes (2.50) at The Curragh on Sunday following her demolition job in a valuable sales race at York last month.

Aidan O'Brien's filly had it all to do after running into trouble on The Knavesmire, but her class prevailed in the end as she ran out a most impressive six-length winner. This is much tougher, of course, as she tackles seven furlongs for the first time on a stiffer track, but I'm confident the Phoenix Stakes winner is up to the task.

Green Empress travelled well when getting off the mark in the Group Two Debutante Stakes over course and distance last month, beating the re-opposing Alpha, Ibelieveicanfly and Dancing Destiny and looks the main danger.

Sandals ready to take a big step forward

The way Starlust hit the line behind US raider Bacio in the Nunthorpe Stakes at York tells me he can run another massive race in the BAR 1 Betting Flying Five Stakes (3.25) at The Curragh.

Ralph Beckett's five-year-old came out of retirement following a fruitless spell at stud and looks to have found the form that won him the Breeders' Cup Turf Sprint two years ago.

TIME FOR SANDALS' last two runs have been solid, and I like the way she flashed home in the Nunthorpe after repeatedly finding trouble mid-race. If things fall her way, she could be the one they all have to beat with Kieran Shoemark in the saddle.

Image: Time For Sandals (centre) is Hollie Doyle's pick in the Flying Five

Sequoia can post a giant run in National

Juddmonte colt Monogram looked a class act when scoring over course and distance for Joseph O'Brien and can take the step up to Group One company in his stride in the Goffs Vincent O'Brien National Stakes (4.00).

One thing he does lack, however, is experience which could give GIANT SEQUOIA the advantage. Aidan O'Brien's first string won the Group Two Futurity Stakes here last time and is clearly a colt of huge potential.

On the evidence of that run, the son of the great Frankel is still open to enough improvement to make his presence felt at the very highest level so gets my vote in a mouthwatering renewal.

Brilliant Scandinavia set for fifth Group One

With a seven-race unbeaten streak to his name, I can't wait to see the brilliant SCANDINAVIA enhance his reputation in the Comer Group International Irish St Leger (4.35) on Sunday.

Aidan O'Brien's Gold Cup winner steps back to one mile and six furlongs which shouldn't be a problem on such a stiff track, and he can justify short odds in his quest for a fifth victory at the highest level.

Stable companion Jan Brueghel, who, like Scandinavia is a Doncaster St Leger winner, is the obvious danger. He looked as good as ever when winning this season's Coronation Cup and won't mind this greater test of stamina.

Sports.title: Norris beats Antonelli with 'masterpiece' to take Spanish GP pole
Sports.content:
Lando Norris produced a stunning lap to beat Kimi Antonelli to the first pole position at Formula 1's all-new Madring circuit in a thrilling Spanish Grand Prix Qualifying.

The McLaren driver hadn't appeared to be in contention for pole at any point of the session, but found a huge amount of pace on his final run to edge out championship leader Antonelli by 11 thousandths of a second.

Max Verstappen, who had surged into pole contention earlier in the session, edged out Lewis Hamilton for third after the Ferrari driver produced a strong recovery having crashed in final practice earlier on Saturday.

Charles Leclerc start behinds his Ferrari team-mate in fifth, while Antonelli's Mercedes team-mate and nearest championship challenger, George Russell, could only manage sixth.

The remarkable nature of Norris' lap was further highlighted by a near-half second gap to his team-mate Oscar Piastri in seventh.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch how Lando Norris took the Spanish Grand Prix pole with this sensational final lap

Norris said: "I'm shocked! A little bit surprised to be here now. My god, that was probably one of the best laps I've done in my career.

"Very, very happy. Very proud, very happy for the team. Just one of those laps where everything came together.

"I had a good idea of what I wanted to do. It was whether my brain let me do it on the last lap. Everything pretty much worked perfectly."

Spanish GP Qualifying: Top 10 1) Lando Norris, McLaren

Red Bull's Liam Lawson, who continues to deputise for the injured Isack Hadjar, was eighth, while Alpine's Franco Colapinto and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10.

A supreme collective display of driving saw the session pass without any of the red-flag stoppages that had been expected at the hugely challenging new circuit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Bearman took a huge hit right at the end of P3 at the Spanish Grand Prix.

Haas driver Oliver Bearman was unable to participate due to the heavy damage done to his car in a big crash in final practice, but there were only kisses rather than heavy contact with the barriers as the field pushed to the limit in qualifying.

With F1 returning to Madrid for the first time since 1981 as the capital city takes over from Barcelona as the Spanish Grand Prix host, the locals were left disappointed as both Williams' Carlos Sainz and Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso were knocked out in Q1.

How Norris painted 'masterpiece'

There had been high expectations for McLaren coming into the weekend given Norris had recorded back-to-back pole positions and race victories either side of the summer break at similar-style circuits before Antonelli won last weekend's Italian Grand Prix.

However, that pace failed to materialise throughout practice, and Norris' personal challenge was severely heightened when he missed almost the entirety of Friday's second session because of a gearbox failure.

Mercedes looked as though they may have it all their own way before Verstappen flashed strong pace in Q2 to suggest he was capable of contending for pole.

Then, Ferrari, who had started the weekend strongly, suddenly rediscovered their pace as Hamilton took provisional pole after the first runs in Q3.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lando Norris describes his lap which claimed him Spanish GP pole as 'one of my best'

A thrilling finale was in store, and it begun with Antonelli displacing Hamilton from pole, before the Brit improved but failed to reclaim top spot.

Attention then turned to Norris and Verstappen, who were both lighting up the timesheet with fast sector times.

Norris had a massive slide in the final corner that almost took him into the barrier. It cost him around two to three tenths of a second, but he still edged out Antonelli.

Verstappen produced the fastest middle sector of the session but couldn't keep up his speed in the final part of the lap and had to settle for third.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Lewis Hamilton reflects on his Spanish Grand Prix qualifying lap, which saw the Ferrari drive secure fourth.

"It was pretty much perfect," Norris reflected. "Bar the last corner, I thought I was in the wall and the boys would have to repair the car tonight.

"It could have been a little bit better - but one of the best laps I've done."

McLaren team principal Andrea Stella shared Norris' assessment that it was one of the best laps of the reigning world champion's career.

"It was a masterpiece," Stella told Sky Sports F1. "We have seen across the whole weekend, if we put it altogether, we are not far from the best cars.

"We worked our way step by step to try to put all the performance together. Lando did it only on the final run in Q3 and in the final corner he made a mistake of three tenths. It was an incredible lap - one of the best of his life until the last corner."

Sports.title: Blackburn see off Millwall
Sports.content:
Dapo Afolayan's brace helped Blackburn secure a much-needed 3-1 win over Millwall at a discontented Ewood Park.

The game hadn't kicked off before the first 'Venky's out' chants could be heard but Afolayan, who turned 29 on Friday, gave the home fans something to cheer with a deft improvised flick to open the scoring in the 41st minute.

Although Lydon Dykes' penalty levelled matters six minutes after the restart, Afolayan's thumping strike around the hour mark restored the lead.

Rovers managed the closing stages well and substitute Andri Gudjohnsen made the game safe in stoppage time with a breakaway goal to end a four-game winless run.

Millwall suffered their third league defeat in four, but will rue the header Dykes planted wide midway through the half.

The Lions made the more assured start but their only chance of note came in the 11th minute when Balazs Toth saved Camiel Neghli's low volley.

Todd Cantwell's snapshot forced Max Crocombe into a smart save but he could do nothing as Rovers went ahead.

Sam Morsy was given too much space just inside the area and though his shot lacked direction, Afolayan's ingenious flick steered the ball into the Millwall net from close range for his first league goal for the club.

The hosts made a disastrous start to the half when substitute Gady Beyuku's first contribution was to bring down Tairyk Arconte in the area after the attacker had stolen in behind on the left.

Dykes took responsibility from the spot and made no mistake, slamming his third of the season down the middle.

But Rovers responded in the 58th minute through Afolayan, who was given time and space to race forward from the centre circle, evading one challenge before rifling a left-foot shot into the bottom corner from 18 yards.

Arconte had the ball in the net after a long throw but the referee saw a foul in the melee.

Millwall continued to threaten and spurned two chances, both created by their full-backs.

First, Zak Sturge's low cross found Arconte, who could only divert wide on the stretch, before Mark Sykes sent in a superb right-wing cross that Dykes headed wide from close range.

Arconte threatened again in the 73rd minute when he turned Tom Atcheson inside out and raced into the area but Hayden Carter crucially deflected his effort over.

Tony Mowbray's side repelled the threats and struck the last blow in a counter started and finished by Gudjohnsen, who shielded the ball and released Jayden Fevrier who squared for the Icelandic striker to slot his third of the season into the bottom corner.
