Sports.title: Resurgent Stoke win at Watford
Sports.content:
Jack McGlynn orchestrated Stoke's first away win since January with a deserved 2-1 success at Watford.

A 1-1 draw at Cardiff in midweek had ended a sequence of nine consecutive defeats away from Staffordshire, and the Potters were good value for their first win in 11 road trips - and their third success in four Championship games.

McGlynn opened the scoring for Stoke on half-time with Eric Bocat doubling the lead 13 minutes into the second half. Amin Nabizada's reply came too late for the Hornets.

Fortified by 10 summer signings, including United States international McGlynn from Houston Dynamo and £10million former Manchester United academy midfielder Ethan Galbraith from Swansea, Stoke were superior until they survived a late scare.

In the opening eight minutes alone Bocat, in plentiful space, sliced wastefully wide from 10 yards out and the French defender's cross was headed down, but over the top, by Lamine Cisse.

Then Galbraith tested home keeper Federico Ravaglia, the Italian making a sharp low save, as Watford struggled to break the Potters' press.

It took the Hornets 35 minutes to register a goal attempt of any description, Othmane Maamma firing a speculative volley way off target to end Stoke's monopoly of 10 shots without reply.

The home side went close when Ukraine international Maksym Talovierov's last-ditch challenge thwarted Mamadou Doumbia, diverting his fierce effort over the top.

But Watford, already depleted by a glut of injuries, were further disrupted by full-back Jordan Zemura's withdrawal before half-time and they could not make it through to the interval unscathed.

Lamine Cisse had already had a goal discounted for offside before McGlynn struck in the last seconds of added time, firing high and handsome beyond Ravaglia from the edge of the box to give the visitors a deserved lead.

Livewire McGlynn, signed on deadline day for a reported £4 million, kept Watford's hard-pressed defence under pressure with his set-piece delivery and his double act with Galbraith was outstanding.

Stoke continued to call the tune after the break, Cisse rattling the underside of the bar before Northern Ireland midfielder Justin Devenny shovelled a glorious chance wide from Ben Johnson's low centre.

But they were on course for the points when Bocat broke through the inside left channel and fired low across Ravaglia into the far corner to double the Potters' lead 12 minutes into the second period.

Watford lacked energy, cohesion and, crucially, options to change the course of the game from the bench, where head coach Alessio Dionisi named two goalkeepers, two right-backs, two centre-forwards and no midfielders among his eight substitutes.

Former West Ham striker Michail Antonio, who signed a one-year deal on Friday, was among Dionisi's replacements but his last appearance in English football was back in December 2024 and he was effectively included as window dressing.

Substitute Nabizada's brilliant, curling 25-yard effort, his third goal of the season, reduced the deficit on the stroke of 90 minutes, and Stoke then had to live on their nerves for six minutes of stoppage time before ending their 251-day wait for an away win.

Sports.title: Swansea see off struggling Burnley
Sports.content:
Swansea moved back into the automatic promotion places as they piled more misery on new Burnley boss Nicky Hayen, whose side slumped to the bottom of the Championship with a 3-1 defeat.

The victory took Vitor Matos' side level on points with West Ham at the top of the table and erased the memory of the 3-1 midweek mauling at Southampton. For Burnley, it was a fourth defeat in seven league games and they are still awaiting their first win.

Both goals they conceded in the first half were avoidable and had their shooting been more precise they could have been at least on level terms.

Hayen was able to include former Leicester and England striker Jamie Vardy in his matchday squad for the first time following the 39-year-old's transfer from Serie A side Cremonese.

He finally made his debut as a 64th-minute substitute and had the ball in the Swansea net nine minutes later only to have the goal ruled out for offside.

Burnley started well enough and the first chance of the game fell to striker Zeki Amdouni in the eighth minute.

Having held off Stephen Welsh in the race for a ball into the Swansea box he then shot into the side-netting from a good angle.

The home side opened the scoring in the 14th minute when Adam Idah grabbed his third goal of the season. Chasing a long ball through the centre he first held off Igor Julio and then ran on to challenge Burnley goalkeeper Max Weiss just outside his box.

Weiss waited too long, lost the ball when challenged by Idah and then had to watch the striker calmly stroke the ball into an empty net.

Worse followed in the 33rd minute after Burnley had had a significant period of pressure.

But when their third corner in a row was cleared, Ugo Raghouber gave the ball away and Elijah Just picked it up in the centre circle before sending Moussa Yeo on a solo run at goal from halfway.

He got to the edge of the area before putting the ball into the bottom-left corner to notch his first goal in a Swansea shirt.

Despite going two goals down, Burnley created a number of chances and Aaron Ramsey forced Lawrence Vigouroux into a brilliant one-handed save as he tipped his rasping shot onto the crossbar.

The visitors finally scored in the 58th minute when Largie Ramazani beat the offside trap and fired past Vigouroux with a low shot into the left corner. That gave the Clarets renewed hope of getting something out of the game, but Swansea added a third goal five minutes later.

Marco Stamenic threaded the ball through for Ronald to chase and after outpacing Lucas Pires he pulled the ball across the box to give Zan Vipotnik the easiest of tap ins.

Burnley had the ball in the Swansea net once again in the 87th minute from an inswinging corner but referee James Bell spotted interference on Vigouroux and ruled it out.

Sports.title: Liverpool held at Anfield as Fulham pick up first point
Sports.content:
Liverpool were held to a frustrating goalless draw as Fulham picked up their first point of the Premier League season at Anfield.

Liverpool, who gave a first Premier League start to Bradley Barcola, were a little sluggish in their use of the ball from the outset after their exertions against Atletico Madrid. Alisson's error was almost punished by Goncalo Garcia but Jeremy Jacquet cleared.

The Reds did come close to the breakthrough when Victor Munoz headed against the crossbar midway through the first half. But Fulham enjoyed plenty of possession despite coming into this in poor form having lost their first three under Alvaro Arbeloa.

They had the clearer chances in the second half too, Josh King forcing Alisson to tip the ball wide before Rodrigo Muniz should have finished when fed by fellow substitute Kevin as Fulham pushed for an unlikely winner. Alexander Isak glanced wide at the other end in stoppage time.

The result means that Andoni Iraola is still searching for his first Premier League win at Anfield and has now drawn three of his first four games in the competition as Liverpool boss. Unbeaten but unsatisfied. The positives here all belonged to the ex-Red Arbeloa.

Sports.title: History! Osborne first woman to win British Classic as Highwayman lands Leger
Sports.content:
Saffie Osborne made history at Doncaster as she became the first female jockey to win a British Classic, steering Highwayman to victory in the 250th Betfred St Leger.

Handed the plum spare ride on the improving Vinnie Roe Stakes winner as just reward for a fine season, the eye was drawn to the 24-year-old who was moving stylishly into contention as the runners entered the long Doncaster straight.

With the Ballydoyle contingent seemingly beaten off as Osborne sent her mount on with a furlong to run, the only danger appeared Billy Loughnane and 5-2 second-favourite Enceladus.

However, Highwayman (11-) was not for reeling in under an inspired Osborne who entered the record books on the 250th anniversary of the world's oldest Classic.

Osborne told ITV Racing: "I don't think I've ever been speechless in my life and I didn't have this on the bingo card for this week.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player An emotional Saffie Osborne was still struggling to come to terms with her achievement after she became the first female rider to win a British Classic.

"I didn't have a ride in the race on Monday morning, let alone one with a chance, and I can't thank so many people enough. Firstly Joseph and his team for putting their faith in me, it won't change Joseph's life, but it will change mine.

"My agent Tony Hind, I would be nowhere without him and I know it's cliched but my mum, dad and whole family. This means the absolute world and as I crossed the line I was in shock. I just can't believe it and it just doesn't feel real.

"I was more forward than I anticipated, but he was travelling so well into it, I couldn't believe it."

Image: Osborne lifts the Leger trophy at Doncaster

Delighted winning owner John Neocleous said: "The horse did it so easy didn't he. I wish I could say more about it, but I'm still in shock!

"This horse was 250-1 in a maiden (at Naas in June), that was the wrong distance of course, but it's amazing how far he has come. We should not be surprised, though, because Joseph keeps on making history.

"You don't know where this horse will end up, but he did win pretty easily today.

"We're going to Australia, I think, but Joseph will make the decisions, he's in charge.

Image: Highwayman leads home a 1-2 for trainer Joseph O'Brien in the Leger, beating stablemate Enceladus

"We won the Galway Plate a month ago with King Alexander so it's been a hell of a summer but this is a different level completely."

Regarding his history-making jockey he said: "Saffie is amazing, I'm sure she's in shock as well.

"Joseph came up with the idea, but he called me first and I was extremely happy to have her, she's an up-and-coming jockey, she knows how to ride a finish and I thought if she rode a good finish maybe we'd be placed. But she won comprehensively so I'm very happy.

Image: Osborne sporting her Leger-winning cap, tailor-made for the 250th running of the race

"I said to Saffie, 'let's go and make and history', but I didn't really believe it!"

O'Brien watched the race from Leopardstown where he told Racing TV: "The two of them are two really nice, progressive stayers.

"It's a special race and he was impressive I thought.

"He was a slow learner and mentally he was immature, but when he got rolling he improved hand over fist.

"Enceladus is a huge big horse and he'll make a smashing four-year-old."

Sports.title: Wolff fumes at 'couch warriors' questioning Mercedes' treatment of Russell
Sports.content:
Mercedes chief Toto Wolff has dismissed suggestions from "couch warriors" that the Silver Arrows failed to treat George Russell fairly during the Italian Grand Prix.

Russell was narrowly leading the race from his team-mate Kimi Antonelli when Mercedes took a decision to pit the Italian under a virtual safety car.

The call ultimately benefitted Antonelli as he used his fresh tyres to pull off a stunning victory having started from 19th on the grid, which increased Russell's deficit to the Italian at the top of the standings to 66 points.

Speaking to Sky Sports F1 ahead of qualifying at this weekend's Spanish Grand Prix, Wolff reiterated his belief that the fact Antonelli was running on a medium tyre and Russell a hard tyre completely justified the decision.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Italian Grand Prix.

"It's absolutely the right thing we did," Wolff said. "He (Russell) was on the hard. It was predicted to be a one-stop as the better strategy.

"The medium was a compromise; we had to put the medium on Kimi because he started on the hard.

"There is just no way, and obviously there are some couch warriors that will drop their comments after having watched some other material online… saying that he was penalised is complete bull****."

'No hidden agenda or favouritism'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli and George Russell go wheel-to-wheel for the Italian Grand Prix lead in several epic team-mate battles.

Russell started the season as the clear title favourite but has been outperformed by Antonelli, with the 20-year-old having dramatically exceeded expectations during just his second F1 campaign.

The Brit backed Mercedes' decision following the race in Monza, insisting that Antonelli deserved credit for his performance.

Wolff admitted that "harsh calls" are required to win championships but insisted that there is no "hidden agenda or favouritism" with his team.

"That's been part of our role in the last 12 years, to manage both sides of the garage well," Wolff said. "Because if you are in a title fight, one is always going to be disappointed after a race and the other one is going to be happy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player George Russell explains why the team chose not to pit him during the VSC, which potentially could have cost him the win in Monza.

"I think as long as you're transparent and there is no hidden agenda or favouritism, then it's the best to manage it.

"But it doesn't mean that we are not making some harsh calls. We are having stern talks on a Sunday morning - what are the various situations we are facing? Behind some pressure from another team, and one of our drivers behind the other one and it's too slow, we're going to invert the cars when it's needed.

"But it's a decision that you need to take sometimes, in either direction by the way, whoever is in front. The decisions you need to take in order to win a championship, but it's always going to be balanced."

'We could have looked like idiots, like Ferrari'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brundle and Rosberg debate who was at fault for the collision between Hamilton-Leclerc.

Ferrari shared the headlines with Antonelli following the Italian Grand Prix after a first-lap incident between Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, which saw the former push his team-mate into the gravel, resulting in the loss of several places.

Wolff said that the clash made Ferrari look "like idiots" but wanted to avoid being overly critical of his rivals given Antonelli and Russell came close to also leaving Mercedes red-faced.

The Austrian said: "I can express my opinion now and say it's not on to push your team-mate off in Turn 2, but three or four laps from the end, we had some scary moments between the two of them that we didn't expect in that way because George had a tyre that was shot, and Kimi was a second quicker.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Toto Wolff weighs in on the Ferrari incident that saw Charles Leclerc push Lewis Hamilton wide during the Italian Grand Prix.

"Did we expect them to fight like they did, which could have ended up with a car in the gravel?

"We could have quickly looked like idiots as well, like the Ferraris looked, eventually, so it's a fine margin."

Sports.title: Hull stun Chelsea with Mohamed Belloumi double before João Pedro rescues a point
Sports.content:
Do not make the mistake of assuming this was a backs-to-the-wall effort from Hull. Their remarkable start to the season goes on and a point was the least Sergej Jakirovic’s side deserved after they pushed Chelsea to the limit in an absorbing game.

This was the first time Chelsea have dominated possession in a league game this season and it did not lead to anything pretty. Xabi Alonso’s attack was contained for long spells, even though goals from Morgan Rogers and João Pedro ended Hull’s spotless defensive record, and the Spaniard’s side remain a mess without the ball. Chelsea are conceding at a rate of two a game and saw their winless run in home games against promoted sides stretched to five after Mohamed Belloumi twice punished defensive errors during the first half.

A rejig from Alonso, whose omission of Maxence Lacroix in central defence enabled a switch from a back three to a 4-2-3-1 system, did not work. It was a bold move from Chelsea’s manager and the early signs were encouraging. Chelsea made a fast start and were ahead after leaving four players forward at a Hull corner in the seventh minute. A scorching counterattacking ended with Rogers taking a pass from João Pedro and smashing a low shot inside Konstantinos Tzolakis’s near post after skipping round Regan Slater on the left.

Hull’s hopes of dragging Chelsea into a grind appeared to be over. Having to chasing an equaliser against the league’s most potent counterattacking seemed less than ideal. It was set up for Chelsea to push for more and they looked comfortable at first, going close to doubling their lead when Pedro Neto drew a save from Tzolakis with a shot from the right.

Perhaps it was too simple for Chelsea. Unable to detect danger, they dozed off when Tzolakis launched a clearance into their own half. Malo Gusto failed to deal with the loose ball and was muscled off it by Ryan Giles. The Hull left-back was able to hook a cross to the far post and when Jorrel Hato misjudged the bounce Belloumi was free to smash a clinical shot past Emi Martínez.

Rattled, Chelsea forgot how to do the basics. They were too open and lacked alertness off the ball. Hull attacked again, another ball from the left causing confusion. Belloumi flicked it on and Lewie Coyle, whose run went untracked by Rogers, saw his low shot deflected behind by Levi Colwill’s goalline clearance.

View image in fullscreen João Pedro fires home Chelsea’s equaliser in the second half. Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA

Still there was no response from Chelsea, who were a mess while trying to deal with the resulting corner. Martínez flapped at the cross, Semi Ajayi headed against the bar and Belloumi was brimming with confidence when the ball dropped to him. The Algerian shot first time and was rewarded for his decisiveness when it beat Martínez thanks to a deflection.

Chelsea spent the rest of the opening period banging their heads against an orange and black wall. Alonso, who inspired a comeback against Leeds in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday by giving his players a half-time rollocking, responded by replacing Hato with Pep Chavarría during the interval.

Hull began the second half in containment mode. The crosses came in but Ajayi and Nobel Mendy were in towering form. Reece James almost equalised, Tzolakis saving the captain’s free-kick, but Chelsea were finding it difficult to create in open play.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The frustration grew, Hull’s timewasting at goal-kicks and throw-ins testing the patience. There was a delay after a nasty clash of heads between João Pedro and Mendy, who made way for Lucas Herrington. It was a setback for Hull but they continued to defend with extraordinary commitment and almost extended their lead. Martínez mishandled a shot from Slater and did well to block from Oli McBurnie on the rebound.

It was a pivotal moment. Chelsea soon levelled, Cole Palmer stirring and lifting his team. The No 10 drove down the left, Hull surprised by the directness, and his cutback was perfectly placed for João Pedro to equalise with a rising shot.

Chelsea still lacked control. Alonso looked to shift the dynamic, Danny Welbeck partnering João Pedro in attack after replacing Gusto. Welbeck’s presence quickly led to a chance for Palmer, who curled over from a promising position. Palmer then found Rogers but Tzolakis denied the £117m man.

Jakirovic continued to show his smarts. Hull’s substitutes gave them a threat. Brooke Norton-Cuffy had a shot blocked after a surge and Mohamed-Ali Cho missed a sitter during the dying stages, shooting straight at Martínez from close range. Hull, who are third, could have nicked it.

Sports.title: Frustrated Liverpool fail to take chances as Fulham claim deserved first point
Sports.content:
In the not-so distant past when they were vying for a right-back role with Spain, Andoni Iraola often lost out to Álvaro Arbeloa. The points were shared at Anfield but the Liverpool head coach was thwarted by his old adversary once again as Fulham deservedly claimed the first Premier League point of Arbeloa’s tenure.

The visitors belied their lowly position and a run of three successive league defeats to take a point from a Liverpool side that represented a pale imitation of their Champions League selves against Atlético Madrid on Wednesday.

Whether it was the after-effects of the win over Diego Simeone’s side, with a quick turnaround between fixtures, or the three changes that Iraola made from the European game, hardly a significant amount, the deterioration in Liverpool’s performance was dramatic. The hosts were sluggish and sloppy in possession – Florian Wirtz and Kostas Tsimikas both put simple passes straight out of play in the first half – and Fulham bypassed their midfield repeatedly. Tsimikas’s return to the starting lineup lasted all of 45 underwhelming minutes.

Another factor in Liverpool’s subdued performance was Fulham’s confidence on the ball and defensive organisation. For a team arriving at Anfield with only defeats to their name in the Premier League this season, the visitors’ belief and willingness to attack was hugely impressive. With more conviction in front of goal, Arbeloa’s side could have capitalised on Liverpool’s slow start.

Bradley Barcola created an early, difficult chance for Alexander Isak with a measured pass behind the Fulham defence. Liverpool’s number nine just missed the far post from a tight angle. Victor Muñoz went closer still with a glancing header from a Dominik Szoboszlai corner. Bernd Leno, the Fulham goalkeeper, reacted superbly to claw the ball away from just under his crossbar. But that was the sum total of Liverpool’s enterprise in the first half, with an attacking quartet that cost almost £400m.

Fulham were gifted a glorious opportunity when Alisson played a ridiculous pass to Ryan Gravenberch when he was under pressure from Sander Berge on the edge of his own area. The loose ball fell to Josh King, catching the eye yet again in the visiting attack, who was sent flying by the Liverpool keeper but the referee Thomas Bramall played a good advantage as Gonzalo García took over. Garcia had time to pick his spot only for Jérémy Jacquet to block his shot in front of the goalline.

View image in fullscreen Jérémy Jacquet clears the ball off the line to deny Fulham the lead. Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPA

The visitors prospered down their left and Oscar Bobb missed another good opening when, unmarked and 18 yards out, he mis-controlled Alex Iwobi’s pinpoint delivery. Jacquet came to Liverpool’s rescue once again seconds later when preventing García breaking through with an excellent challenge. Antonee Robinson would head wide before the interval from Bobb’s right wing cross.

Liverpool were deserving of a few home truths during the break – chiefly, you would have been slaughtered for this last season under Arne Slot – and did perform with greater intensity and purpose in the second half. But not with any more threat. The introductions of Cody Gakpo, Alexis Mac Allister and Milos Kerkez brought a measure of improvement but Fulham continued to contain the hosts comfortably. Calvin Bassey in particular had a commanding game against Isak.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visitors remained dangerous on the counterattack and Alisson pushed away a King effort that was heading for the top corner after the forward had cut inside Jacquet to create space for himself. His replacement, Rodrigo Muniz, also let a decent chance run away from him inside the area and the substitute Kevin dragged a shot wide from 18 yards.

Isak finally escaped Bassey’s attentions in stoppage time to flick Szoboszlai’s corner wide of the far post from close range. There was still time for one more Liverpool raid when Jeremie Frimpong escaped down the right and crossed through the heart of the Fulham box. The ball struck Rio Ngumoha and sailed over, leaving Liverpool with a third draw from four league games at the start of Iraola’s reign.

Sports.title: London City’s superstars brought down to earth in WSL defeat at West Ham
Sports.content:
West Ham claimed their first Women’s Super League win of the season with a 2-1 home victory over London City Lionesses.

Kelly Gago put the Hammers ahead after 21 minutes, racing between the centre-backs Mapi León and Isa Kardinaal to latch on to Seraina Piubel’s pass from nearly halfway and rounding Elene Lete in the London City goal. Lete, who signed from Real Sociedad in 2025, remains Eder Maestre’s first choice in goal despite the arrival of the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps this summer.

Daniëlle van de Donk was denied an equaliser when Constance Picaud-Inconnu saved low, with another of London City’s big-name summer signings Alexia Putellas lifting the rebound over the bar under the challenge of Inès Belloumou.

View image in fullscreen Kelly Gago is congratulated after scoring the opener. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

Viviane Asseyi scored doubled West Ham’s lead three minutes after the break after being released by Riko Ueki, running the length of the London City half before firing home.

London City set up a frantic finish after Van de Donk’s clever backheel from Kadidiatou Diani’s low cross crept in at the near post 14 minutes from time.

View image in fullscreen Danielle van de Donk flicks home for the Lionesses. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

The veteran Netherlands forward had scored a similar goal with the winner against Manchester United on the opening weekend – this defeat at Chigwell Construction Stadium was a reality check for Maestre’s side as they look to challenge the top teams in the WSL this season.

West Ham bounced back after their opening-weekend defeat to Tottenham. “I saw the spirit that I want to see every time, it’s part of our identity,” said their head coach, Rita Guarino. “We can’t forget that we have this kind of value and we need to show it in every single game.”

Sports.title: Igor Jesus and Liam Delap strike for Forest to deepen Aston Villa’s league woes
Sports.content:
This summer there were a couple of significant pieces of the puzzle for Oliver Glasner to put into place at Nottingham Forest. The first was a mobile striker to lead the line, and the other was a wing-back to fit his favoured 3-4-3 system. Enter Liam Delap and Daniel Munoz, both of whom had a big say in Forest’s first win of the season, though the match-winner was one of the old guard in Igor Jesus. Delap registered his first Forest goal in style, a powerful shot from 25 yards and Munoz was involved in the slick move that saw Igor Jesus read Morgan Gibbs-White’s exquisite backheel to down Aston Villa, who remain winless in the Premier League.

Unai Emery hoped a Champions League victory at Club Brugge on Tuesday would be the catalyst to ignite their Premier League campaign but Igor Jesus clinched victory late on, after Alysson, a half-time substitute, headed in the equaliser. Emery introduced Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi for their Villa debuts just after the hour but it was Forest’s £45m record signing Delap who ended the game victorious, this a typically boisterous display from the former Chelsea striker. Glasner tried to sign Delap for Crystal Palace last summer and finally has his man.

For so long it seemed Villa would be left to ruminate on the few clear chances they created, chiefly the slapstick episode that saw Matz Sels somehow deny Victor Lindelof and Murillo smacking his attempted clearance against his own post. Sels denied Lindelof with his feet and after the ball cannoned off a post the Sweden defender side-footed the rebound into the goalkeeper’s face. Lindelof had scored one goal in almost six years, the last against Luton for Manchester United in November 2023.

Villa were rattled by Forest seizing the lead 45 seconds into the second half. Murillo dispossessed Emiliano Buendia, snapping into a challenge after Boubacar Kamara’s flick and then Delap jinked clear of Ross Barkley. Delap’s next couple of touches took the ball out of his feet, dribbling diagonally across the pitch, before sending a stinging right-foot shot into the Villa net.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap (right) opened his account for Nottingham Forest with a 46th-minute strike. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

Emery sent on Mbaye and Manzambi in place of Buendia and Barkley, culpable for Delap’s goal and both of whom found the going tough, but their arrivals did not bring instant success. Instead Delap thought he had doubled his tally, only for the offside flag and a subsequent VAR check to show he strayed offside when latching on to Morgan Gibbs-White’s neat cross . A few moments earlier Tyrone Mings, a first-half substitute for the injured Pau Torres, made a desperate block to thwart Dan Ndoye after superb holdup play by Delap.

Villa levelled on 74 minutes, the 20-year-old winger Alysson, a January signing from Gremio, feasting on some slack marking after a short-corner routine. John McGinn, the Villa captain, floated a dainty right-foot cross in from the left flank and Alysson eluded Murillo to send a header past a hapless Sels. A powerful Mbaye strike, kept out by Sels, was the catalyst for the corner.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Glasner had been readying Igor Jesus when Villa scored but the striker still arrived to replace Ndoye. Villa Park was primed for a big finale but Forest also roused. Zion Suzuki clambered down to his right to keep out Xaver Schlager’s header and then Igor Jesus popped up to strike the winner. Munoz exchanged passes with Gibbs-White, who eliminated three Villa defenders with a sumptuous flick before Igor Jesus coolly rolled the ball past Suzuki. Glasner whirled around on the touchline wagging his index finger and the celebrations continued in the away end long after the final whistle.

Sports.title: Championship roundup: Birmingham sink Derby, West Brom held by QPR
Sports.content:
Callum Styles earned West Brom a point as they came from behind to draw 1-1 against QPR at The Hawthorns. It meant they failed to regain their position on top of the table after West Ham beat Wrexham 6-0 on Friday.

A Chris Mepham own goal put QPR in front in the 38th minute but that lead lasted three minutes as Styles equalised to extend West Brom’s unbeaten home record to 11 games.

The home side had slightly more of the chances but against the run of play Rangers took the lead. Kwame Poku sent Rumarn Burrell racing clear and he turned his man before forcing Max O’Leary into a diving save, only for the rebound to hit Mepham on the head and bounce into the unguarded net.

West Brom levelled when Styles, who was playing in an unfamiliar right-back role, curled home a low shot from just outside the area.

Substitute Thierry Gale headed a 90th-minute winner as Bolton ended a run of four successive Championship defeats with a 1-0 victory over Cardiff. The Barbados international stole in at the far post to convert a left-wing cross from Theo Bair.

Cardiff would have shared the spoils but for some excellent work by the Bolton goalkeeper, Gavin Bazunu.

Paik Seung-ho scored his first goal since December to give Birmingham a 2-1 victory over Derby at Pride Park. Bobby Clark put Derby ahead only for Carlos Vicente to reply two minutes later and Paik won it after a lengthy stoppage for what looked like a serious injury to Derby’s Henrik Meister.

Sports.title: Febrile Manchester derby awaits amid growing rift between United fans and club
Sports.content:
Manchester United’s nine victories from 10 Premier League games at Old Trafford in 2026 cast their stadium as a fortress Manchester City aim to ransack on Sunday, to join Leeds in departing with three points during this calendar year.

Michael Carrick has overseen the division’s highest home points-per-game return in that span: 2.7, ahead of Arsenal’s 2.27 (from 12 matches) and Manchester City’s 2.25 (11); and his side have scored the most goals: 26, to City’s 23, and the champions’ 20.

When Enzo Maresca’s side motor across town, the 199th edition of a local squabble that draws a riveted global audience will be as febrile as ever – on and off the pitch.

A United fan group, the 1958, has called for a “peaceful protest” before kick-off, starting at a pub near the stadium, against what it believes is disproportionate action in the club’s drive to eradicate ticket touting. United said on Friday that 685 accounts had been subject to a ban and 464 supporters had received a reduced sanction or final warning.

Then, when the whistle blows, United will attempt to end City’s perfect start of four victories in all competitions, improve a disappointing return of four points from three league games and repeat the opening result of Carrick’s second interim tenure, achieved in January four days after his appointment: a 2-0 downing of Pep Guardiola’s visitors in which Bryan Mbeumo and Patrick Dorgu were on target.

A 2-1 defeat by Leeds on 13 April is the sole blemish on United’s league record at Old Trafford since. The sequence shows how impressive Carrick’s stewardship has been and last month’s 5-2 hammering of Ipswich came in his first home game as the permanent manager.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes has been integral to Manchester United’s recent success at Old Trafford. Photograph: Allstar Picture Library Ltd/Richard Sellers/Apl/Sportsphoto

Scan the results of his 10 away league games and you find four wins (at Arsenal, Everton, Chelsea and Brighton), four draws (West Ham, Bournemouth, Sunderland and Everton) and two defeats (Newcastle and Hull): 16 points from 30, compared with 27 from 30 when United play in front of their crowd.

A major factor behind the home record is easy to identify: Bruno Fernandes. In the 10 Old Trafford games the 31-year-old has provided 10 assists and scored five times. Without the captain Carrick’s team would surely struggle, as his hat-trick against Ipswich underlined.

Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha have been key support acts, scoring four goals each (Cunha also has two assists), and Benjamin Sesko has impressed with five goals at an average of one every 70.8 minutes.

United’s rearguard is the achilles heel: 13 goals conceded in the 10 home matches (Arsenal have allowed seven, City nine) is hardly parsimonious, so on Sunday the visitors will hope to prosper by hogging the ball, stymieing the opportunity for fast breaks that Mbeumo, Fernandes, Cunha and Sesko thrive on, and going at pace at the creaky defence.

City did not do this enough in Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League victory at Porto, perhaps because Elliot Anderson was stood down, and perhaps, too, because Maresca’s nascent team are in the work-in-progress phase.

View image in fullscreen Elliot Anderson has settled quickly at Manchester City after his £116m move from Nottingham Forest. Photograph: Dave Thompson/AP

Anderson has looked a natural schemer since his £116m transfer from Nottingham Forest, running contests. In last Saturday’s 1-0 win over Coventry his display was Rodri-esque: a big call, but no exaggeration as the 23-year-old sprayed passes around, snuffed out danger, demanded to be found when under pressure and showed a spurt of speed to escape traffic.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United have their own midfield lieutenant: Kobbie Mainoo, who has started nine of the 10 home league games under Carrick, scoring once and assisting once. The match he missed? The Leeds reverse, which is surely no coincidence because the 21-year-old’s ability to mould time and space is priceless in the hurly-burly of the 100mph Premier League – as his masterclass versus Ipswich reiterated.

Harry Maguire calls the lad from Stockport United “midfield monster” so in the showdown between Mainoo and Anderson we may witness the derby’s defining battle – and the future of England’s engine room.

A United victory would send those of the red persuasion home happy, bragging rights secured in the workplace and local hostelries. But an underlying discontent will remain: at the longstanding grievance regarding the Glazers’ ownership that has haemorrhaged resources and saddled the club with a near £1.3bn debt, and at the recent initiative designed to eliminate the black market resale of tickets.

It is a worthy act but the accusation from fans is of a draconian approach. In July United began contacting supporters who used six or more devices to access accounts linked to the club or to forward tickets, on the basis this suggested the potential buying of seats to resell. Those in question were asked why multiple accounts were accessed, to identify the differing devices used, and for photo ID to prove validity.

A joint statement by six fan groups complained “of longstanding supporters who have followed Manchester United for decades, often across multiple generations of the same family, being treated as suspects”.

The dispute continues. On Tuesday the 1958 said: “Supporters are now facing serious sanctions which can remove their right to attend matches. We believe nobody should face such action without being told clearly what they are accused of and being shown the evidence used to justify it. If there is clear, substantive evidence of serious wrongdoing or organised ticket touting, show it. No loyal supporter should be treated as guilty without being given a fair opportunity to understand and challenge the case against them.”

United said that in addition to the sanctions and warnings, they had identified 1,617 accounts that required further review owing to “unusual activity”.

So before the derby will be the latest protest against the latest issue that shows the fracture between proud institution and proud fanbase. Against this backdrop Carrick hopes to extend United’s proud home record – which viewed through the prism of the disconnect between club and supporters is particularly impressive.

Sports.title: Football lends voice to message worth relaying: men should talk about their pain | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
If you watched US television adverts during the World Cup for any length of time one thing just kept leaping out. I’ve mentioned this before here, but it still seems both jarring and significant. Every third or fourth rotation in that endless daytime scroll, in between the Chicken Megadeth Hyper-Box Family Meal Deal, either side of David Beckham expertly consuming a light beer, is an advert for antidepressants.

The format for these is always the same kind of thing: contented, wholesome people throwing frisbees, or strolling through a small-town antiques fair, while a warm, honeyed, reassuring voiceover talks about how horrifying their lives are, with the suggestion that only a lengthy course of Smileothorium can solve this.

In another world there would be a call to study this phenomenon, to consider why a nation of such dazzling abundance and opportunity should also feel glazed, worthless and deprived of hope. But this is not that world. More than 50 million Americans have depression. This is demand and supply in action, a battle for market share in a £6bn industry. The US often worries about itself in its post-industrial age. What are we now? What can we still make? Where is the new frontier? Well, human misery is looking pretty hot right now.

The reason for talking about this here is that English football is doing a good thing this week. Between 4-14 September the Premier League is sponsoring the Together Against Suicide campaign. Harry Kane and Prince William have spoken warmly in support. The league is posting words of solidarity on its X account, which is probably not the best way to cheer yourself up if we’re being honest.

This is simple, useful messaging. It applies to people of any age, sex or background. But it applies in particular to men, and to middle-aged men, who are more likely to die by suicide than any other age group. Middle-aged men are more likely to experience depression and anxiety in those years. They can be hard to reach because this often happens out of sight or, most heartbreaking of all, without any indication there was even a problem.

It might be a little blunt in its styling. But what football is doing here is unequivocally good. Nothing else has the same level of reach and cut-through. If one person in the line of that message is touched by it, this seems like a happy outcome.

I think I have locus standi to talk about this. Everyone does. It’s universal. But I’m also unarguably a middle-aged man. I have two sons who are also now men. I have middle-aged male friends, many of whom are, with all due respect, a bit loopy. And like so many other people I’ve been down that road some of the way.

Life in Covid really did it for me. Exhaustion, isolation, the inescapable fact of having to carry on existing. Do you really have to, though? This kind of thing can creep into your mind like a shadow, just another idle thought. Until at some point you realise there’s a shadow in the corner of the room, a ghost in the chair, and it’s talking to you.

The fact is, it’s hard to be a man at any age. Or at least, it’s hard in a way that is distinct from other forms of hardness. And yes this statement might fail to draw an overwhelming wave of sympathy, but this is part of the problem. Pain comes for everyone. There’s no hierarchy of suffering. And male pain, male alienation is often carried around like a dead weight for exactly this reason.

double quotation mark Being able to talk about this stuff is the direct opposite of weakness. There is always someone willing to do this with you

As you get older this can be related to a sense of obsolescence. Men want to do stuff. There’s a kind of programming to feel useful, to serve some kind of function. Frankly, most middle-aged men would be happier if someone just gave them a big piece of wood and told them to saw it in half, then at the end of the day told them they’ve done a really good job, they’re good boys and everyone’s proud of them. Tomorrow you can come back and put it together again.

Instead it can feel like every part of the world is independently conspiring to make you feel like crap. Diminishing work, vanished usefulness, isolation, the way life can exhaust you quietly, without any obvious trauma. Men are not good at processing this. The key method, the strategy we’ve worked out over the years is: don’t process it at all. Carry on. Keep running through the red zone. Lads, it’s not a long-term plan.

I have two pieces of aged wisdom on this front. First, the obvious one. Embrace the feeling and talk about it. Sounds like a cliche. Is actually true. Feeling bad isn’t some deeper, truer version of you. The good stuff also exists and is just as real. Both will pass, and pass again.

Small things do help. Muscular, loud, well‑meaning men on the internet are actually right. Don’t eat rubbish. Get outside. Speak to other people. Remember that the sun also rises, that feeling terrible is also evidence of the ability to feel good. Prince William is right: being able to talk about this stuff is the direct opposite of weakness. There is always someone willing to do this with you, who will like and admire you even more as a result.

The second thing is: you do also have to fight. Those outmoded forms of masculinity – being stoic, resisting your own feelings – tend to get a bad rap. But everyone needs a bit of this. The problem is men are often not taught anything else to go with it.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Sport in Focus Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Life is brutal. It will come for you. It is heroic to fight this, even more so when you’re suffering. Old English poetry is full of epic tales shot through with melancholy warriors weeping at the sadness of the empty hall. In Roman culture the ability to embrace melancholy and fear – as well as scything off the limbs of your enemies – was seen as a sign of great and crowning masculinity. Scipio burnt Carthage to the ground, then sank into a massive depression, at which point he was seen as even more masculine, even more thrillingly in touch with his depths.

View image in fullscreen Prince William makes a speech at Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium on World Suicide Prevention Day. Photograph: Shirlaine Forrest/PA

Letting it out is strong. Would you like to be a Viking? Or a Roman hero with a sword? Well, those guys spent half their lives in a state of profound inner doubt, telling people all about it, then feeling so much more able to ride off on a horse and do something ostensibly useful.

There is something worth saying about sport in the middle of this. I was at Arsenal last weekend and before kick-off a bubbly and cheerful voice announced: “Suicide is NOT inevitable!” as though what we’re talking about here is having dandruff or not drinking enough water. The messaging is good. The messaging is great. The messaging is also, let’s be honest, an attempt to soothe the effects of the world in which big sport thrives and makes its fortunes. Is this a nice place?

It isn’t hard to work out why American TV is so full of adverts for antidepressants. Take a look at the stuff in between. Terrible, degrading food. Consumer goods you don’t need but must be made to crave. Pills to get you off that addiction to opioids we’ve already given you. Endless excitable messaging from corporations that secretly hate you.

Big Sport does not exist outside of this world. It is part of the same system. Oh, now you care about sad middle-aged men? The same ones who can’t afford to go any more, who feel alienated from what was once a bit of a lark and a chance to get together, whose brains must be subjected to the curated rage of the online idiot-scape?

The note of regret here is that sport still has so much power to be warm, to act as a source of contact. Witness for example the rush of love a few years back when Ben Stokes was able to talk about being depressed while simultaneously operating at his peak as England captain. It felt like a message no one had ever really sent in the same way, that you can feel like this and still be OK, or even heroically functional; that feeling all those things is really just a part of feeling.

In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org

Sports.title: ‘Atrocious’ – Chelsea make unwanted 65-year history as ex-Premier League boss left stunned
Sports.content:
Hull City became the latest club to breach Chelsea's fragile defence and condemn the west London club to an unwanted record.

Mohamed Belloumi's 28th-minute leveller ensured the Blues have now gone 20 league games without a clean sheet for the first time in 65 years.



3 Hull's leveller ensured Chelsea reached the defensive milestone

The Blues reached the unwanted feat in Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Hull at Stamford Bridge.

It is the first time they have conceded two or more goals in the first four matches of a league campaign in ten years as well.

Xabi Alonso’s side were aiming to banish the memories of last weekend’s defeat at Arsenal and started in blistering fashion.



Morgan Rogers’ expertly-taken finish fired Chelsea into a seventh-minute lead but some suspect defending handed Hull a way back into the match.

A hopeful ball into the box was misjudged by Jorrel Hato, allowing Belloumi to fire the Tigers level.



Chelsea, who have conceded three times in two of their three home games in all competitions this season, once again showed their defensive frailties and talkSPORT co-commentator Steve Bruce issued his own scathing assessment.

Defensive flaws

“Absolutely atrocious from Chelsea,” Bruce said on Game Day Live. “A long punt up the middle. They haven’t dealt with that one for a start.



“Then it’s gone into the corner flag, then they haven’t stopped the cross coming in.

“The cross is one of these looping things that’s come into the box.

“Hato’s misjudged it badly, got underneath it, bounced over the top of him and there was Belloumi to strike it with his left foot and give the ‘keeper no chance.

3 The Chelsea boss was seen deliberating with his side as they chased a leveller Credit: Getty

“It’s the first time they’ve been anywhere near Chelsea’s goal, I can’t remember the goalkeeper touching the ball but they’ve got themselves level.”



Things got even worse for Alonso’s men just six minutes later when Belloumi lashed home from the edge of the box to fire the Premier League new boys in front.

Chelsea got themselves back on level terms in the 66th minute when Joao Pedro produced a neat finish after good work from Cole Palmer down the left.

But there is plenty of work to do for Alonso and his shaky backline who conceded three in the midweek Carabao Cup win over Leeds.

The Spaniard lined up against Hull with a back four comprising of Hato, Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill and Malo Gusto.



The midweek cup goalfest followed Sunday's 2-1 defeat at Arsenal and the 4-3 win over Brighton.

3 Joao Pedro rescued a point for his team with a well-taken finish

The Blues set the tone for a potentially leaky campaign by shipping twice in their season opener at Fulham.

Chelsea's only clean sheet this season came in the 2-0 Carabao Cup victory over Luton Town last month.

Sports.title: Sorba Thomas makes Premier League appearance one day after rollover car crash
Sports.content:
Sorba Thomas was brought on for Hull City against Chelsea a day after being involved in a rollover crash.

Images of the Wales winger's car upside down on a residential road spread across social media on Friday morning.

2 Thomas has returned to the pitch following his crash Credit: Getty

Hull later revealed that Thomas, who was signed from Stoke City in a £10million deal, escaped was 'completely unscathed'.

He was named in their matchday squad for the Premier League trip to Chelsea, with the 27-year-old featuring as a substitute.

Hull boss Sergej Jakirovic opted to bring him on for Elliot Stroud in the 60th minute of the 2-2 draw at Stamford Bridge.

It was his second league appearance for the Tigers, with the first coming in the 0-0 draw with Aston Villa last weekend.

Many were surprised to see him in action given the state of his car just over 24 hours ago.

Chelsea and Hull battle for draw

Thomas entered play as Hull led 2-1 courtesy of two goals from Mohamed Belloumi.

But Joao Pedro brought Chelsea level, having assisted Morgan Rogers for their opener earlier in the match.

Chelsea became the first side this season to score against Hull, who did not concede versus Manchester United, Coventry City or Villa.

However, the Tigers remain unbeaten on their top flight return and have the joint-best defence with Arsenal and Leeds United.

They are third in the table and may well have dismissed any fears over relegation back to the Championship.

2 Chelsea and Hull shared the points in a tight contest Credit: AFP

As it stands, Hull could be in contention to qualify for Europe later in the season.

It would be a remarkable story for a club who last played Premier League football before the current campaign in 2016/17.

Chelsea on the other hand are a point behind them in fourth and have conceded at least two goals in every leage match.

The reverse fixture at the MKM Stadium is scheduled for March 20.

Sports.title: Morgan Rogers joins elite Chelsea group just four league games into Blues career
Sports.content:
Morgan Rogers joins elite Chelsea group just four league games into Blues career

Morgan Rogers continued his stunning start to life at Chelsea with yet another goal.

The club-record £117million signing from Aston Villa found the target inside six minutes of the 2-2 draw with Hull City on Saturday.

2 A fine strike from Rogers put Chelsea ahead at home to Hull Credit: Getty

Rogers was fed the ball from Joao Pedro, and then fired low into the bottom corner to hand Chelsea an early lead.

He has joined an elite group of Chelsea heroes who have scored or assisted in each of the first four Premier League games of a season.

Didier Drogba was first to do so in the 2010/11 campaign as he netted four and assisted four.

Cesc Fabregas followed him with six assists in 2014/15, as Diego Costa scored seven in that same run.

Costa also bagged four goals and an assist in 2016/17, and then Eden Hazard hit two goals and two assists at the start of 2018/19.

Hull then equalised shortly before the half-hour mark as Mohamed Belloumi struck after some poor Chelsea defending.

The Algerian scored a second moments later as the visitors fought back to lead.

However, Joao Pedro was on hand to score a second for Chelsea by thumping into the roof of the net.

Rogers goals and assists for Chelsea so far

On his Premier League debut for the club, Rogers scored for Chelsea in their 3-2 victory against west London neighbours Fulham.

He then assisted Pedro Neto as they beat Brighton 4-3, before hitting an early opener in the 2-1 loss at Arsenal.

2

Rogers' goal against Hull came after he came off the bench and assisted three times in the 6-3 Carabao Cup win over Leeds United.

Whilst their attacking quality was on show once again, Chelsea still have concerns over their defence.

They have conceded two goals in all of their matches this season bar one, the 2-0 Carabao Cup win over Luton Town.

Saturday's result at home to Hull has left them fourth in the table and a point behind their opponents.

Sports.title: Derby player stretchered off in neck brace after lengthy stoppage as manager gives update
Sports.content:
Derby player stretchered off in neck brace after lengthy stoppage as manager gives update

Derby striker Henrik Meister was stretchered off in a neck brace after going down off the ball during the clash with Birmingham.

The worrying scenes unfolded at the start of the second half at Pride Park, as the Dane went to ground, causing play to be temporarily halted.



4 Meister received immediate medical attention after going down with no one near him

4 The striker was stretchered off the pitch and was seen in a neck brace

Appearing to have suffered a head injury, medical staff immediately came on to the pitch, before a stretcher was called for.

A seven-minute delay followed, as Meister received treatment, with it becoming clear the player would be unable to continue.



Meister was ultimately moved onto a stretcher and was carried off the pitch to a standing ovation from both sets of fans.

Reporting the incident at the time, Derby wrote on X: "A lengthy delay at the start of the half as Meister goes down off the ball and is stretchered from the field.



"We're all with you, Henrik."

Meister 'OK', says Derby boss

After the match, which saw Birmingham claim a 2-1 win, Derby boss John Eustace revealed Meister was in a stable condition, and said he will undergo concussion protocols.

Giving an update, Eustace said: "To lose him just after half-time was tough.



"It was difficult, but he's OK now. He's having concussion protocols. We'll just have to see how he is. I've been speaking to him and he seems okay."

Meister had been making his first start for Derby after being handed his debut in a 3-0 Championship defeat at West Ham last weekend.

The 22-year-old joined the club on a season-long loan from Serie B side Pisa less than two weeks ago.

4 Henrik Meister joined Derby this summer



With the score at 1-1 at the time of Meister's substitution, Birmingham went on to take the lead through Paik Seung-ho on 64 minutes.

The Rams went in front on 40 minutes, as Bobby Clark fired in from a tight angle.

But Birmingham hit back immediately, as Carlos Vicente equalised less than two minutes later.

The Blues opted for an early substitution at half-time, as manager Chris Davies brought Paik on for Jhon Solis in midfield.



And the switch paid off almost instantly, as the South Korean headed home from Liam Millar's corner.

This proved to be the winning goal, as Birmingham held on to their lead even through 13 minutes of second-half injury time, largely due to Meister's injury.

4 John Eustace is navigating a tough start to the season

The result leaves Derby still in the Championship relegation zone, as they remain 21st in the table.



John Eustace's side have made a disappointing start to the campaign which has seen them win just once.

The Rams have lost six of their opening seven league matches, as well as claiming a draw against Cardiff in their second game.

As for Birmingham, victory moves them into eighth place on 10 points, with this the last of the Championship play-off places following the league's decision to expand this last term.

Sports.title: Evangelos Marinakis appoints manager considered by Tottenham and Bournemouth
Sports.content:
Tottenham and Bournemouth both came close to appointing new Olympiacos head coach Imanol Alguacil, talkSPORT understands.

Alguacil took charge of the Greek giants earlier this week, as he was chosen by Nottingham Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis to succeed Jose Luis Mendilibar following his brief tenure.

5 Imanol Alguacil takes charge of Olympiacos having built a strong reputation in Spain

In a manner which has become familiar, Marinakis axed Mendilibar just seven matches into the new season.

The departing manager became the 25th coach dismissed by the Greek businessman, who also owns Forest and Rio Ave, in 16 years.

Hours later, his successor was revealed to be Alguacil, who carved out a strong reputation during his seven years in charge of Real Sociedad.

The 55-year-old led the Basque outfit between 2018 and 2025, during which time he won the Copa del Rey in 2020 – the club’s first trophy in 34 years.

Having taken on Sociedad as a mid-table LaLiga outfit, Alguacil went on to European qualification in five consecutive seasons - reaching the last 16 of the Champions League and Europa League.

Premier League interest

With Alguacil building an impressive CV in Spain, talkSPORT can reveal this led to him being considered by Premier League clubs.

After the Spaniard left Sociedad at the end of the 2025/26, Tottenham explored the possibility of hiring him before ultimately settling on Thomas Frank.

This proved an ill-fated appointment, with Frank lasting just eight months in charge while Spurs went on to narrowly avoid relegation.

And more recently, talkSPORT understands Bournemouth identified Alguacil as a candidate for their head coach vacancy this summer.

With the tactician spending seven months at Saudi Pro League side before departing in February, the Cherries shortlisted him among their managerial options after Andoni Iraola's departure.

5 Evangelos Marinakis bought Olympiacos in 2010 Credit: Getty

5 Spurs and Bournemouth kept tabs on Alguacil after he left Real Sociedad and had a brief spell in charge of Al Shabab

Marco Rose instead took charge at the Vitality Stadium, and is searching for his first win after setting an unwanted Premier League record in his first three games.

Alguacil is also understood to have been high up on Liverpool's list of options, with his work at Sociedad ranking him highly in their data, before Iraola ultimately took the role.

And while the Spanish coach missed out on a Premier League role, he is said to have been sold on the project at new club Olympiacos.

Discussions centred on their sporting project - with Marinakis' goal to compete strongly in Europe and the opportunity for Alguacil to build something rather than simply taking the next available job.

Rated by Mourinho and Enrique

As well as being considered for major vacancies, Alguacil's rising stock has seen him earn praise from some of football's leading managers.

Alguacil’s record of 153 wins and 95 losses in 330 matches at Sociedad led to the legendary Jose Mourinho admitting he struggled to find a weakness in his team after facing him as Roma manager.

5 Alguacil's only managerial silverware so far is the 2020 Copa del Rey with Real Sociedad

5 Real Madrid boss Mourinho was full of praise for Alguacil when the pair faced off in 2023 Credit: Getty

Speaking in 2023, the ex-Manchester United and Chelsea boss said: “It’s difficult to find weaknesses in Real Sociedad.

"Imanol is a very good coach; he has a very well-prepared team.

“In addition to the quality they have, they are also capable of changing systems from one match to another or even during the same game.”

Mourinho isn't his only admirer, with PSG's back-to-back Champions League-winning boss Luis Enrique also claiming Sociedad played the most impressive best in LaLiga under Alguacil.

After facing Alguacil's Sociedad, Enrique said: “What a great team, what a way to compete!

“They are wonderful. I’ll tell you something: Real Sociedad is the Spanish team that plays the best football, without any doubt. Imanol Alguacil deserves congratulations.”

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta is not crazy for sabotaging Arsenal’s pre-season – it’s completely right
Sports.content:
Dean Saunders has defended Mikel Arteta after the Arsenal boss revealed he deliberately disrupted his side's match preparations during pre-season.

The Gunners were affected by air traffic control issues as they travelled to Italy to face Napoli in their Champions League opener.



4 Arteta's Arsenal are looking to win the Champions League this season after losing in the final last term Credit: Getty

Delays flying out of London Luton Airport on Tuesday meant that Arteta's side arrived in Italy around three hours behind schedule.

Arsenal managed to put this behind them on the pitch, as they earned a deserved 1-0 win at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona.

And Arteta later said his team had been unaffected by the disruption because of his methods used in pre-season.



In his press conference ahead of the Gunners' trip to Sunderland, he said: "I love those challenges and I try to create them in pre-season. So when they happen, we have already experienced them and we are ready.

"So, get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.



"It can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there is so much traffic, and I don't want the players and the staff panicking so when that happens, adapt to it.

"When that happens, adapt to it. We have two or three hours on the plane - can we use it? Play together, spend some time together, sleep.



"But don't complain or use it as an excuse because it's not helpful at all."

Arteta's methods defended

Reacting to the news on talkSPORT, ex-Liverpool and Wales striker Saunders defended Arteta's outside-the-box methods, pointing to his own experiences as a manager.

"Having managed myself, I can understand where he's coming from," Saunders said.

4 Arteta opened up on his most recent outlandish method in a recent press conference



4 The Gunners seemed to benefit from their preparations, as Martin Odegaard's goal sealed victory over Napoli Credit: Getty

"Because basically as a manager... I'll put it in a nutshell. Your job is to sign good players, get them fit, give them a plan with and without the ball and keep the discipline. Those are the basics.

"So what you try and do as a coach is eliminate every single excuse a player can throw at you. Because they will. Players find an excuse for everything.

Saunders continued: “Fitness levels to start with, they've got to be fit. And the physio treatment. So we're all fit.



“Training intensity - because they'll start throwing that one in. Is the hotel nice? Yes. Is the food that we're serving you up nice? Yeah. Have I given you a plan all week? Yes.

“So everybody's ready. No excuses. Get over that white line. Do not come in this dressing room and give me excuses. That's the only thing you can do for players - put them on the pitch and say, 'Go on then, I've set everything up for you'.

"That's what he's trying to do. He's trying to get in their heads and say, 'No excuses lads'."

4 Arteta has overseen Arsenal's 100 per cent start to the season Credit: Getty



Arteta's past innovations

This isn't the first time Arteta has made the headlines with his unusual methods to get the best out of his Arsenal side.

In the 2022 All or Nothing Amazon documentary covering the club, the Gunners boss famously prepared his team for an away trip to Anfield by blasting Liverpool's 'You'll Never Walk Alone' anthem on loudspeakers during training.

For another game, Arteta used a lightbulb in a pre-match team talk - as he wanted his players to shine and emit energy to one another.

Then in 2024, he hired professional pickpockets to steal items from his players during a team dinner, which was used as a lesson to teach them to stay alert.



Arteta's outlandish methods appeared to have rubbed off on his players too when, in April, a fire was lit at the club’s London Colney training ground by the team in an attempt to rouse themselves for their Champions League clash with Sporting Lisbon.

Former Liverpool defender Alvaro Arbeloa returns to Anfield on Saturday as his Fulham side take on the Reds.

Arbeloa played 98 games for Liverpool from 2007 to 2009, featuring 66 times in the Premier League during that stint.

4 Arbeloa is returning to Anfield as a manager after spending two years there as a player Credit: Getty

He's now going to be back on Merseyside, hoping to come out on top against his old side and pick up a much-needed win.

Fulham have lost their first three games in the Premier League this season, with boss Arbeloa still waiting on three points.

That has the Cottagers sitting 19th in the table heading into this clash, so they will be desperate for a victory.

History, however, doesn't give Arbeloa much chance of glory on his return to Anfield.

Three previous Liverpool players have taken on the club as a manager in the Premier League, but none of them have won.

Paul Ince was in charge of Blackburn in 2008 when his side were beaten by the Reds, while Mauricio Pellegrino lost twice to his old club when managing Southampton in 2017/18.

And most recently, club icon Steven Gerrard lost both of his meetings with Liverpool with Aston Villa in the 2021/22 campaign.

Can Arbeloa put an end to that losing streak? He'll hope to do so, particularly to Fulham's dismal start to the season.

Sports.title: Chelsea 2-2 Hull City: Joao Pedro salvages a point for Xabi Alonso's side as high-flying Tigers continue their rampant return to the Premier League
Sports.content:
Chelsea 2-2 Hull City: Joao Pedro salvages a point for Xabi Alonso's side as high-flying Tigers continue their rampant return to the Premier League

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea got the three goals needed to defeat Fulham 3-2, and the four required to beat Brighton 4-3, but this time, the awesomeness of the attack did not outweigh the direness of the defending.

We knew it would catch up with Chelsea eventually. It simply isn’t sustainable, relying on outscoring the opposition every single week. Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro got a goal apiece so that Xabi Alonso could avoid losing to Sergej Jakirovic’s streetwise Hull side, at least.

But Chelsea cannot continue in this way, as thrilling as it all is. They have ‘JPMorgan’ up top, but a piggy bank at the back, waiting to be smashed open at the slightest knock, as it was twice here.

Do not let the ball bounce. It is defending 101. The no-no we are all taught as children when we dream of making it as a professional player, like Jorrel Hato is for Chelsea today.

Yet Hato broke that basic rule. He let the ball bounce in front of him and loop over him after it was launched into the box from the left wing by Ryan Giles, with Malo Gusto having failed to stop that from happening. While Hato was watching, Mohamed Belloumi was waiting, there behind him to blast beyond Emiliano Martinez and make it 1-1.

Hato was hooked at half-time for good reason. This 28th-minute equaliser made it 20 Premier League matches in succession that Chelsea have failed to secure a clean sheet. Their last one arrived in a 2-0 win over Brentford in January, in what was Liam Rosenior's first league match as head coach as he kickstarted his doomed tenure.

Chelsea have ‘JPMorgan’ up top, but a piggy bank at the back, waiting to be smashed open at the slightest knock, as it was twice here

Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro got a goal apiece so that Xabi Alonso could avoid losing to Sergej Jakirovic’s streetwise Hull side

That leveller injected belief into Hull. Sergej Jakirovic’s visitors were in the ascendancy from then on, and they scored again in the 34th minute after yet more Looney Tunes defending from Chelsea. Emiliano Martinez was flapping as Hull’s corner came in. Semi Ajayi headed into the crossbar. The rebound fell to Belloumi, who, via two deflections which made Chelsea’s six-yard box resemble a pinball machine, scored for 2-1.

The Hull fans loved it, of course. ‘We’re top of the league,’ they sang. ‘We’re gonna win the league,’ they added. ‘Sorba Thomas, he parks where he wants,’ they chanted in a nod to their winger who crashed his car on the way into the training ground this week. Despite flipping his Land Rover Defender upside down, Thomas escaped without harm, and came on as a substitute here.

Their formidable start to this season is no fluke. They are a solid, organised side who play to their strengths, though it was always going to be a tall task for Hull to hold on to their 2-1 lead.

That is because we know how good Chelsea’s attackers are. They had scored within the opening five minutes of their first three Premier League fixtures against Fulham, Brighton and Arsenal.

This time it took a little longer – six minutes and 16 seconds via Rogers – but it put Chelsea into a strong position until their defence undid them. While trailing 2-1, it took Cole Palmer carrying the ball down the left before setting up Joao Pedro for Chelsea to equalise. It was a fine finish from the Premier League’s player of the month; precisely what we have come to expect from the Brazilian.

Chelsea searched for their late winner with Alonso going for it, throwing on Danny Welbeck and Estevao. But Hull, with their low block, were solid. The visitors held firm and so, after riding their luck in wins over Fulham and Brighton, Chelsea’s defence finally cost them.

Sports.title: UFC great hurls racial slurs at officers and turns on his fans in new footage from public intoxication arrest
Sports.content:
WARNING: VIDEO CONTAINS GRAPHIC LANGUAGE
