World.title: Gucchi marmik, millet pulao, khumb galouti: What's on the Brics gala dinner menu
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi's gala dinner for Brics leaders and other visiting dignitaries is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on Saturday evening, following the first day of the Brics Summit.

The dinner is expected to conclude in the next 10 to 15 minutes.

The evening features a specially curated Indian menu showcasing regional flavours and traditional preparations, along with a cultural performance by an ensemble of more than 100 artistes from India and other Brics member countries.

Whatâs on the dinner menu

The gala dinner features a specially curated Indian menu that brings together regional flavours, traditional recipes and contemporary interpretations of Indian cuisine.

The meal begins with Khandvi Mille - Feuille, a steamed gram-flour roll tempered with mustard, coconut and curry leaves, served with Kesar mango, micro-greens and yoghurt dressing. The starters also include Khumb Galouti, tender pan-grilled mushroom kebabs with mint pearls, served on a bed of sheermal bread.

The main course features Paneer Lababdar, soft cottage cheese cubes simmered in a rich gravy of shallots and tomato, alongside Gucchi Marmik, Himalayan morel mushrooms and tender asparagus gently simmered with saffron, raisins and mamra almonds.





Other dishes on the menu include Carrot Bean Poriyal, made with carrots and green beans toasted in aromatic South Indian spices in hand-pressed virgin coconut oil and finished with freshly grated coconut. Thakkali Belle Saaru, a light lentil broth of toor dal enriched with fresh tomatoes and curry leaves, is also being served, along with Millet Pulao, Beetroot Raita and assorted Indian breads.

The dessert selection includes Old Delhi Fruit Cream with Jalebi, pairing seasonal fruits and lightly whipped cream with a crispy sweet fritter, and Shahtoot Phirni, a slow-cooked pudding of milk and rice topped with sweet mulberries and gold leaf.

âBrics Symphonyâ at gala dinner

The dinner is being accompanied by âBrics Symphonyâ, a cultural performance featuring an ensemble of around 160 artistes, with Indian dancers and musicians forming the core of the troupe.

Indian artistes are performing classical dance forms including Bharatanatyam, Kuchipudi, Odissi and Kathak, representing different regions of the country. Traditional Indian instruments are also being featured alongside musicians from other Brics member countries.

The performance, being coordinated by the Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), is expected to run for around 20 to 25 minutes and will include intermittent vocal renditions.

Dinner follows packed first summit day

The gala dinner comes after a busy opening day of the BRICS Summit, which brought together Chinese President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and other world leaders and senior dignitaries in New Delhi.

World.title: 'Mera saaya saath hoga': Congress takes jab at Centre, says Nehru's Bandung spirit shaped Brics declaration
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress on Saturday took a jab at the Centre by invoking the iconic Bollywood melody, âTu jahan jahan chale ga, mera saaya saath hoga,â to highlight former Prime Minister

's diplomatic legacy and its presence in the newly adopted Brics New Delhi Declaration.

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh pointed to Paragraph 16 of the declaration, which recalls the 1955 Asian-African Conference in Bandung, Indonesia, and its principles of equality, independence, non-intervention and mutual benefit.

"Para 16 of the New Delhi Declaration just adopted at the Brics Summit says the following: 16. We recall 1955 Asian-African Conference in Bandung, Indonesia that proclaimed general principles, including equality, independence, non-intervention, and mutual benefit.â

"We stress that the Bandung Spirit serves as a reference in the pursuit of a fairer, more inclusive, and representative multilateral system," he added.

Jairam said the reference to Bandung in the Brics declaration showed how Nehru's vision for the Global South continues to resonate in contemporary diplomacy.

"Here are some jottings by Jawaharlal Nehru on the afternoon of April 22, 1955, at that historic meeting.





Vineet Thakur recently wrote a fine piece on these and other jottings, doodles and notes of Nehru at Bandung. Remember that old Bollywood hit song Tu jahan jahan chale ga, mera saaya saath hoga," said the Congress leader.

The Congress leader's reference to Bandung comes as Brics leaders push for reforms in global governance and greater representation for developing countries.

Drawing on historian Vineet Thakur's analysis of Nehru's notes from the 1955 Bandung Conference, Jairam highlighted how the handwritten records captured the behind-the-scenes tensions and negotiations at the historic gathering.

Nehru's notes included his observations on the length of speeches, including Carlos Romulo's 31.5-minute address, as well as his writings in Urdu, Hindi and English.

The notes also recorded details that were not reflected in official accounts, including Ahmed al-Shukeiri's speech on Palestine, which helped place the issue within the emerging Global South agenda, ANI reported.

Nehru also used the same airline pad slips to draft a tribute to Albert Einstein.

Einstein had written to Nehru shortly before his death, urging him to engage with Chinese premier Zhou Enlai at Bandung to help ease tensions between China and the US over nuclear weapons.

Earler in the day, the Brics countries adopted the New Delhi Declaration 2026, supporting the aspirations of India and Brazil to play a greater role in the United Nations, including its Security Council.

China and Russia, both permanent members of the UN Security Council, reiterated their support for India's and Brazil's aspirations.

Brics leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to reforming the Security Council to make it more democratic, representative, effective and efficient, with greater representation for developing countries.

The declaration strongly condemned the April 2025 terror attack in Jammu and Kashmir and called for zero tolerance towards terrorism.

On trade, the bloc expressed serious concern over the growing use of unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures, saying they distort trade, threaten global supply chains and create uncertainty for international economic activity.

Brics also reaffirmed support for reform of the World Trade Organisation and called for an open, equitable, transparent, fair, inclusive and rules-based multilateral trading system. It called for the immediate restoration of a fully functioning two-tier binding WTO dispute settlement mechanism.

In April 1955, representatives of 29 Asian and African governments gathered in Bandung, Indonesia, to discuss peace, economic development, decolonisation and the role of the developing world during the Cold War. The conference's core principles included political self-determination, respect for sovereignty, non-aggression, non-interference in internal affairs and equality.

The Brics New Delhi Declaration was adopted at the 18th Brics Summit, being hosted by India. India's chairship is guided by the theme, âBuilding for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability.â

World.title: 'Differences should not become disputes': PM Modi says India-China ties should be guided by 3 mutuals
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese president Xi Jinping on Saturday reaffirmed the need to take a âstrategic and long term perspectiveâ of India-China ties, while stressing border peace, adherence to existing agreements and a âfair, reasonable, and mutually acceptableâ resolution of the boundary question, the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said.

The two leaders met in New Delhi on the sidelines of the Brics Summit and âwelcomed the steady progress in India-China bilateral relationsâ since their last meeting in Tianjin in August 2025.

âDifferences should not become disputes,â PM Modi said, stressing that both sides must be guided by three principles â âmutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interestâ.

According to the MEA, PM Modi emphasised that âpeace and tranquility in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relationsâ.

He also underlined the need for both countries to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues.

The two leaders âexpressed commitmentâ to a âfair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution of the boundary questionâ, with the process to proceed from the political perspective of their overall bilateral relationship and the long-term interests of the two peoples, the MEA said.





The meeting also covered efforts to expand people-to-people ties. Both sides âunderscored the need to further promote cultural exchanges, business linkages and greater mobilityâ between India and China.

On economic and trade relations, the leaders agreed on the need to address each otherâs concerns, including the âstructural trade imbalance and supply chain issuesâ, while facilitating âmeaningful and predictable market accessâ.
